title.zh: 卷一百四十八 列傳第三十五: 董俊 嚴實
title.en: Volume 148 Biographies 35: Dong Jun, Yan Shi
title.raw: 卷一百四十八 列傳第三十五: 董俊 嚴實 Volume 148 Biographies 35: Dong Jun, Yan Shi

sentences.zh: 董俊子文蔚 文用 文忠 文直

translations.literal: Dong Jun—sons: Wenwei, Wenyong, Wenzhong, Wenzhi
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jun—his sons Wenwei, Wenyong, Wenzhong, and Wenzhi

sentences.zh: 董俊字用章，真定藁城人。

translations.literal: Dong Jun, courtesy name Yongzhang, was a native of Gaocheng in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jun, whose courtesy name was Yongzhang, came from Gaocheng in Zhending Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少力田，長涉書史，善騎射。

translations.literal: In youth he worked the fields; as he grew he studied books and history and was skilled at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he farmed; in manhood he took up learning and history and became adept at horsemanship and the bow.

sentences.zh: 金貞祐間，邊事方急，藁城令立的募兵，射上中者拔為將。

translations.literal: During the Jinyou reign of Jin, frontier affairs were urgent; the magistrate of Gaocheng, Li Li, raised troops—whoever hit the mark in archery would be promoted to commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinyou period of Jin, when the frontier was in crisis, Magistrate Li Li of Gaocheng raised levies and promised command to anyone who shot through the target.

sentences.zh: 衆莫能弓，獨俊一發破的，遂將所募兵迎敵。

translations.literal: The crowd could none draw the bow; Jun alone with one shot struck the bull's-eye, and then led the troops he had raised to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: No one else could bend the bow; Jun alone hit the mark at first shot, then led his recruits against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 歲乙亥，國王木華黎帥兵南下，俊遂降。

translations.literal: In the yihai year the prince Muqali led troops south; Jun then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In yihai (1215) Prince Muqali marched south, and Jun submitted.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以勞擢知中山府事，佩金虎符。

translations.literal: In jimao, for his merit he was promoted to administer Zhongshan prefecture, wearing the golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In jimao (1219) he was promoted for distinguished service to provisional governor of Zhongshan and given a golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 金將武僊據真定，定武諸城皆應僊。

translations.literal: The Jin general Wu Xian held Zhending; the cities of Ding and Wu all responded to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Wu Xian occupied Zhending, and the towns of Ding and Wu followed him.

sentences.zh: 俊率衆夜入真定，逐僊走之，定武諸城復去僊來附。

translations.literal: Jun led his men by night into Zhending, drove Xian to flight, and the cities of Ding and Wu again abandoned Xian and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Jun led his force into Zhending by night, drove Wu Xian out, and the Ding-Wu region towns once more broke with Xian and rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 庚辰春，金大發兵益僊，治中李全叛中山應之。

translations.literal: In spring of gengchen Jin greatly sent troops to reinforce Xian; administration vice-commissioner Li Quan rebelled at Zhongshan in response.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of gengchen (1220) Jin poured reinforcements into Wu Xian's camp, and Vice Commissioner Li Quan of Zhongshan turned rebel in his support.

sentences.zh: 俊軍時屯曲陽，僊銳氣來戰，敗之黃山下，僊脫走。

translations.literal: Jun's army was then encamped at Quyang; Xian came in high spirits to give battle; Jun defeated him below Yellow Mountain, and Xian escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's troops were encamped at Quyang when Wu Xian attacked in force; Jun routed him below Yellow Mountain, and Xian fled.

sentences.zh: 獻捷于木華黎，由是僊以窮降。

translations.literal: He presented the victory to Muqali; thereby Xian, brought to extremity, surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the victory to Muqali, and Wu Xian, driven to desperation, submitted.

sentences.zh: 木華黎承制授俊龍虎衛上將軍、行元帥府事，駐藁城。

translations.literal: Muqali, acting by imperial commission, appointed Jun General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and acting commander of the marshal's headquarters, stationed at Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial commission Muqali made Jun General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and acting commander of the marshal's headquarters, with his base at Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 俊嘗謁木華黎曰：「武僊黠不可測，終不為我用，請備之。」

translations.literal: Jun once called on Muqali and said, "Wu Xian is crafty and unpredictable; in the end he will not serve us—please take precautions against him."
translations.idiomatic: Jun once told Muqali, "Wu Xian is treacherous and cannot be trusted; he will never truly serve us. Please guard against him."

sentences.zh: 木華黎然其言，承制授左副元帥。

translations.literal: Muqali approved his words and, by commission, appointed him Left Vice Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali agreed and, by commission, appointed him Left Vice Marshal.

sentences.zh: 陞藁城縣為永安州，號其衆為匡國軍，事一委俊。

translations.literal: Gaocheng county was elevated to Yong'an Prefecture; his troops were styled the Army for the Restoration of the State, and all affairs were entrusted to Jun alone.
translations.idiomatic: Gaocheng was raised to Yong'an Prefecture, his troops were named the Army for the Restoration of the State, and Jun was given full authority.

sentences.zh: 己酉，僊果殺都元帥史天倪，據真定以叛，旁郡縣皆為僊守。

translations.literal: In jiyou Xian indeed killed the chief marshal Shi Tianni, seized Zhending in rebellion, and neighboring prefectures and counties all held out for Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In jiyou (1229) Wu Xian murdered Chief Marshal Shi Tianni, rebelled at Zhending, and the surrounding prefectures and counties all fell to him.

sentences.zh: 俊提孤軍居反側間，戰士不滿千人，拒守永安。

translations.literal: Jun led a lone army amid hostile territory; his fighting men numbered fewer than a thousand, yet he held Yong'an in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jun held Yong'an with a bare thousand men, cut off amid enemies on every side.

sentences.zh: 僊攻之期年，無所利，乃縱兵蹂禾稼，俊呼語之曰：「汝欲得民，而奪之食，無道賊不為也。」

translations.literal: Xian besieged him for a full year without profit, then let his troops trample the grain fields; Jun called out to him, "You wish to win the people yet seize their food—no bandit without principle would do this."
translations.idiomatic: After a year of siege Wu Xian gained nothing and sent his men to trample the crops; Jun shouted across the lines, "You want the people's loyalty yet steal their grain—only a lawless brigand acts thus."

sentences.zh: 僊慚而去，俊出兵掩擊之，僊敗走。

translations.literal: Xian withdrew in shame; Jun sallied forth in ambush and Xian was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Wu Xian withdrew; Jun struck from cover and drove him off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 久之，俊復夜入真定，僊走死，乃納史天倪弟天澤為帥。

translations.literal: After long time Jun again entered Zhending by night; Xian fled and died; he then installed Shi Tianni's younger brother Tianze as commander.
translations.idiomatic: In time Jun again entered Zhending by night; Wu Xian fled to his death, and Jun installed Shi Tianni's younger brother Tianze as commander.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，會諸軍圍汴。

translations.literal: In renchen the allied armies gathered to besiege Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In renchen (1232) the allied armies converged to besiege Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 明年，金主棄汴奔歸德，追圍之；

translations.literal: The next year the Jin ruler abandoned Bian and fled to Guide; they pursued and besieged him;
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Jin emperor abandoned Bian for Guide; the Mongols pursued and laid siege;

sentences.zh: 金兵夜出，薄諸軍於水，俊力戰死焉，時年四十有八。

translations.literal: Jin troops came out by night and pressed the allied armies at the water; Jun fought with all his strength and died there, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Jin forces sortied by night and pressed the allies at the river; Jun fought to the death. He was forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 俊早喪父，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Jun lost his father early and was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Jun lost his father young and was renowned for devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 歲時廟祭，非疾病，跪拜必盡禮；

translations.literal: At seasonal temple sacrifices, unless ill he always performed the full kneeling and bowing rites;
translations.idiomatic: At the seasonal sacrifices he observed every kneeling and bowing rite unless illness prevented it;

sentences.zh: 子雖孩乳，亦使之序拜，曰：「祀，以孝先也，禮宜如是。」

translations.literal: even sons still at the breast he made take their turn in bowing, saying, "Sacrifice takes filial piety first; ritual ought to be thus."
translations.idiomatic: even nursing infants he made bow in turn, saying, "Worship begins with filial piety—the rites demand no less."

sentences.zh: 待族親故人，皆有恩意；

translations.literal: Toward kinsmen and old friends he always showed kindness;
translations.idiomatic: He treated clan kin and old friends with steady kindness;

sentences.zh: 里夫家僮，亦接之有道。

translations.literal: even village laborers and household servants he received with proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: even village laborers and household servants he addressed with propriety.

sentences.zh: 克汴時，以侍其軸為賢，延歸教諸子。

translations.literal: When Bian was taken he regarded Shiqi Zhou as worthy and brought him home to teach his sons.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Bian he esteemed Shiqi Zhou and brought him home to instruct his sons.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「射，百日事耳；

translations.literal: He once said, "Archery is a matter of a hundred days;
translations.idiomatic: He said once, "Archery is mastered in a hundred days;

sentences.zh: 詩、書，非積學不通。」

translations.literal: the Odes and Documents cannot be understood without accumulated study."
translations.idiomatic: the Odes and Documents require years of study before they yield their meaning."

sentences.zh: 屢誡諸子曰：「吾一農夫耳，遭天下多故，徒以忠義事人，僅立門戶。

translations.literal: He repeatedly admonished his sons, "I am but a farmer who, meeting a troubled age, served others with loyalty and righteousness and barely established our household.
translations.idiomatic: He often warned his sons, "I am only a farmer who, in a time of turmoil, served with loyalty and barely raised this house.

sentences.zh: 深願汝曹力田讀書，勿求非望，為吾累也。」

translations.literal: I deeply wish you to work the fields and read books, not seek improper advancement, and become my burden."
translations.idiomatic: Work the land, read your books, and do not reach beyond your station—that would be my ruin."

sentences.zh: 俊忠實自許，不為夷險少移，臨陣，勇氣懾衆，立矢石間，怡然若無事，雖中傷亦不為動。

translations.literal: Jun held himself to steadfast loyalty and did not shift in fortune or danger; in battle his courage awed the host; standing amid arrows and stones he was serene as if nothing were amiss, and even when wounded he did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Jun prided himself on steadfast loyalty unmoved by fortune or peril; in battle his courage awed all ranks, and amid flying arrows and stones he stood serene, unmoved even when wounded.

sentences.zh: 每慕馬援為人，曰：「馬革裹屍，援固可壯。」

translations.literal: He always admired Ma Yuan and said, "To be wrapped in horsehide after death—Yuan was indeed a stalwart."
translations.idiomatic: He admired Ma Yuan and said, "To die on campaign and be wrapped in horsehide—there was a man."

sentences.zh: 故戰必持矛先士卒，或諫止之，俊曰：「我人臣也，敵在前，不死，乃趨安脫危乎！」

translations.literal: Therefore in battle he always took spear in hand ahead of the troops; when some urged him to stop, Jun said, "I am a subject; with the enemy before me, if I do not die, shall I run to ease and escape danger!"
translations.idiomatic: In every fight he led with spear in hand; when men urged caution he replied, "I am the emperor's servant; with the enemy before me, how can I seek safety and leave danger to others?"

sentences.zh: 先是，戊子歲，朝於行在，諸將獻戶口，各增數要利，吏請如衆，俊曰：「民實少而欺以數多，他日上需求無應，必重斂以承命，是我獨利，而民日困也。」

translations.literal: Earlier, in the wuzi year, he attended court at the mobile headquarters; the generals presented household registers, each inflating the numbers for profit; the clerks asked him to follow the crowd; Jun said, "The people are truly few yet we deceive with inflated numbers; later when the court demands and we cannot supply, they will surely levy heavily to meet the order—then I alone profit while the people daily suffer."
translations.idiomatic: In wuzi (1228), at the mobile headquarters, commanders inflated household counts for profit; clerks urged Jun to follow suit. He refused: "The people are few; if we lie about their numbers, the court will demand more than we can supply and levy them into ruin. I alone would profit while they starve."

sentences.zh: 行元帥府時，狂男子三百餘人期日作亂，事覺，戮其渠魁，餘並釋之。

translations.literal: While acting at the marshal's headquarters, more than three hundred madmen plotted rebellion on a set day; when the plot was discovered, the ringleaders were executed and the rest all released.
translations.idiomatic: At the marshal's headquarters more than three hundred men plotted a rising; when exposed, only the ringleaders were executed and the rest freed.

sentences.zh: 深、冀間妖人惑衆，圖為不軌，連逮者數萬人，有司議當族，俊力請主者，但誅首惡。

translations.literal: Between Shen and Ji sorcerers deluded the masses and plotted sedition; those arrested in succession numbered tens of thousands; the authorities proposed exterminating whole clans; Jun strongly petitioned the chief official to execute only the chief evildoers.
translations.idiomatic: Between Shen and Ji, sorcerers stirred the people to sedition; tens of thousands were arrested and officials proposed clan extermination; Jun pleaded that only the ringleaders be put to death.

sentences.zh: 永安節度使劉成叛降武僊於威州，俊下令曰：「逆者一人，餘能去逆，即忠義士，與其家財，仍奏官之。」

translations.literal: Yong'an military commissioner Liu Cheng rebelled and went over to Wu Xian at Weizhou; Jun issued an order: "The rebel is one man; the rest who abandon rebellion are loyal subjects—I will give them their household goods and still memorialize for their offices."
translations.idiomatic: When Commissioner Liu Cheng of Yong'an defected to Wu Xian at Weizhou, Jun proclaimed, "One man rebelled; whoever leaves him is loyal—I will restore their property and recommend them for office."

sentences.zh: 衆果去成降。

translations.literal: The crowd indeed abandoned Cheng and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The troops abandoned Cheng and submitted.

sentences.zh: 沃州民寨天臺為盜，既破降之，他將利其子女，欲掠之，俊曰：「城降而俘其家，仁者不為也。」

translations.literal: At Wo Prefecture the people of Zhai Tiantai were bandits; after they were defeated and surrendered, other generals coveted their women and children and wished to plunder them; Jun said, "To take captives from families when a city has surrendered—no humane man does this."
translations.idiomatic: When bandits led by Zhai Tiantai in Wo Prefecture surrendered, other generals meant to seize their families; Jun said, "A humane commander does not plunder those who have submitted."

sentences.zh: 衆義不取。

translations.literal: The host, moved by righteousness, took nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The troops, shamed, took nothing.

sentences.zh: 南征時，人多歸俊願為奴者，既全其家，歸悉縱為民。

translations.literal: On the southern campaign many wished to become Jun's bondsmen; after he had preserved their households, he released them all as free commoners.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign many offered themselves as his bondsmen; once their families were safe he freed them all.

sentences.zh: 鄰境人有被掠賣者，亦與直贖還之。

translations.literal: People in neighboring districts who had been seized and sold he also redeemed at fair price and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He also paid fair ransom for people seized and sold in neighboring districts and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 其天性之美類如此。

translations.literal: His innate goodness was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the quality of his nature.

sentences.zh: 俊器度弘遠，善戰而不妄殺，故人樂為之用。

translations.literal: Jun's breadth of mind was far-reaching; he was skilled in battle yet did not kill recklessly, so men gladly served him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's vision was broad; he fought well yet seldom killed, and men were glad to follow him.

sentences.zh: 大小百戰，無不克捷。

translations.literal: In great and small battles he was never without victory.
translations.idiomatic: In a hundred battles large and small he was never defeated.

sentences.zh: 為政寬明，見人善治田廬，必召與歡語，有惰者，則怒罰之，故其部完實，民惟恐其去也。

translations.literal: In government he was lenient and clear-sighted; seeing someone who farmed well he would summon him for friendly talk; the lazy he would angrily punish—thus his district was sound and the people feared only that he might leave.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was lenient and clear; he praised diligent farmers and punished the idle, so his district prospered and the people dreaded only his departure.

sentences.zh: 贈翊運效節功臣、太傅、開府儀同三司、上柱國，封壽國公，諡忠烈。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Shou with the posthumous name Loyal and Fierce, with titles including Meritous Minister Who Supports Fortune and Shows Fidelity, Grand Tutor, Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Duke of Shou, styled Loyal and Fierce, with the title Meritous Minister Who Supports Fortune and Shows Fidelity, Grand Tutor, and Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 加贈推忠翊運效節功臣、太傅、開府儀同三司、上柱國，改封趙國公。

translations.literal: Further posthumous honors added the title Meritous Minister Who Pushes Loyalty and Supports Fortune and Shows Fidelity, Grand Tutor, Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Pillar of the State, and changed the fief to Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Later honors added Meritous Minister Who Pushes Loyalty and Supports Fortune and Shows Fidelity and changed his fief to Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 子文炳、文蔚、文用、文直、文忠，文炳自有傳。

translations.literal: His sons were Wenbing, Wenwei, Wenyong, Wenzhi, and Wenzhong; Wenbing has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Wenbing, Wenwei, Wenyong, Wenzhi, and Wenzhong; Wenbing has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 文蔚字彥華，俊之次子也。

translations.literal: Wenwei, courtesy name Yanhua, was Jun's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei, whose courtesy name was Yanhua, was Jun's second son.

sentences.zh: 重厚寡言，不事嬉戲，立志勤苦，讀書忘倦。

translations.literal: He was grave and sparing of speech, did not engage in play, set his will on diligence, and read until he forgot weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Grave and sparing of speech, he shunned idle play, applied himself to study, and read until weariness left him.

sentences.zh: 及長，善騎射，膂力絕人。

translations.literal: When grown he was skilled at riding and archery and his physical strength was unmatched among men.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood, he excelled at riding and archery and possessed matchless strength.

sentences.zh: 事母至孝，接人謙恭，凡所與交，貴賤長幼，待之無異；

translations.literal: He served his mother with utmost filial piety and received others with humble courtesy; all with whom he associated, high or low, old or young, he treated without distinction;
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply filial toward his mother and humble with all he met, treating high and low, old and young, without distinction;

sentences.zh: 至於一揖，必正容端體，俛首幾至于地，徐徐起拱，人所難能。

translations.literal: even in a single bow he would compose his countenance and body, bow his head nearly to the ground, and slowly rise in salute—what others could scarcely achieve.
translations.idiomatic: in a single bow he composed his bearing, bent nearly to the ground, and rose slowly in salute—conduct few could match.

sentences.zh: 兄文炳為藁城令，厲精於政，家務悉委之，凡供給祭祀賓客之事，無不盡心。

translations.literal: His elder brother Wenbing was magistrate of Gaocheng and applied himself zealously to government; household affairs he wholly entrusted to Wenwei, who in all provisions for sacrifice, guests, and the like showed utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Wenbing, magistrate of Gaocheng, devoted himself to office and entrusted all household affairs to Wenwei, who managed sacrifices and guests with perfect care.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，起民兵南征，文炳命文蔚率十有七人，私整鞍馬衣甲，自為一隊，與衆軍渡淮。

translations.literal: In xinchou militia were raised for the southern campaign; Wenbing ordered Wenwei to lead seventeen men; they privately fitted saddles, horses, and armor, formed their own unit, and crossed the Huai with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: In xinchou (1241) militia marched south; Wenbing ordered Wenwei to lead seventeen men who equipped themselves as a private squad and crossed the Huai with the host.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，世祖收大理，還駐六盤山。

translations.literal: In jiayin Kublai took Dali and returned to encamp at Liupan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In jiayin (1254) Kublai conquered Dali and encamped at Liupan Mountain on his return.

sentences.zh: 文炳以文蔚孝謹公勤，可委以事，解所佩金符以讓，帝嘉賞之，授藁城等處行軍千戶。

translations.literal: Wenbing, because Wenwei was filial, careful, and diligent in public duty and could be entrusted with affairs, removed his own golden tally and yielded it to him; the emperor praised this and appointed Wenwei marching chiliarch of Gaocheng and neighboring districts.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing, finding Wenwei filial, careful, and fit for trust, gave him his own golden tally; the emperor approved and made Wenwei marching chiliarch of Gaocheng and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 南鎮鄧州，與荊、襄接境，沿邊城壁未築。

translations.literal: He was stationed south at Deng Prefecture, bordering Jing and Xiang; along the frontier the walls had not yet been built.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted south at Deng Prefecture on the Jing-Xiang frontier, where the border walls were still unbuilt.

sentences.zh: 是年冬十一月，修光化；

translations.literal: That year in the eleventh month of winter he repaired Guanghua;
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the eleventh month, he repaired Guanghua;

sentences.zh: 乙卯，立毗陽；

translations.literal: in yimao he established Piyang;
translations.idiomatic: in yimao (1255) he established Piyang;

sentences.zh: 丙辰，築棗陽。

translations.literal: in bingchen he built Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: in bingchen (1256) he built Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 文蔚悉緫之，治板幹，具畚鍤，儲餱糧，運木石，程其工力，時其饑飽，藥其疾病，見執役者，常以善言撫之，弗事威猛。

translations.literal: Wenwei oversaw all of it: prepared planks and timbers, supplied hoes and baskets, stored rations, transported wood and stone, measured out labor, timed meals, tended the sick, and when he saw those at work always comforted them with kind words, never relying on harsh authority.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei directed everything—timber, tools, rations, stone, labor schedules, meals, and medicine—and spoke kindly to every worker rather than ruling by fear.

sentences.zh: 衆咸感曰：「他將領役，鞭箠怒辱，不恤困苦。

translations.literal: The masses all said with feeling, "Other commanders leading labor whip and insult in anger without regard for hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The laborers said among themselves, "Other commanders beat and insult us without pity.

sentences.zh: 今董侯慈惠若此，我曹安忍負之。」

translations.literal: Now Lord Dong is so kind and gracious—how can we bear to fail him."
translations.idiomatic: But Lord Dong treats us with such kindness—how can we fail him?"

sentences.zh: 各盡力成之。

translations.literal: Each gave his utmost and completed the work.
translations.idiomatic: Each gave his utmost until the work was done.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，攻襄，樊城南據漢江，北阻湖水，卒不得渡。

translations.literal: In dingsi they attacked Xiang; Fancheng south of the Han River and north blocked by lake water—the troops could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: In dingsi (1257) they attacked Xiangyang; Fancheng lay south of the Han with lakes to the north, and the army could not cross.

sentences.zh: 文蔚夜領兵士，於湖水狹隘之處，伐木拔根，立於水，實以薪草為橋梁，頃之即成，至曉，師悉渡，圍已合，城中大驚異之。

translations.literal: Wenwei by night led soldiers to a narrow place on the lake, felled trees and uprooted roots, set them upright in the water, packed them with brushwood for a bridge, and in a moment it was done; by dawn the whole army had crossed, the encirclement was complete, and the city was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei led men by night to a narrow stretch of lake, drove pilings of felled trees packed with brush, bridged the water in hours, and by dawn the whole army had crossed; the city was thunderstruck.

sentences.zh: 文蔚復統拔都軍以當前行，奪其外城，論功居最。

translations.literal: Wenwei again commanded the Badu army in the van, seized the outer city, and in reckoning merit ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: He again led the Badu vanguard, took the outer city, and ranked first in merit.

sentences.zh: 己未，憲宗伐宋，入川蜀，文蔚奉詔，將鄧之選兵西上，由褒斜歷劍閣，而劍、閬諸州，平地不能守，置州事於山。

translations.literal: In jiwei Möngke Khan attacked Song and entered Sichuan; Wenwei received the edict and led Deng's picked troops west, by Baoxie and through Jianmen Pass to Jian and Lang prefectures; the level ground could not be held and prefectural administration was placed on the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei (1259) Möngke invaded Song and entered Sichuan; Wenwei led Deng's picked troops west by Baoxie and Jianmen Pass; in Jian, Lang, and neighboring prefectures the plains could not be held and government was set on the heights.

sentences.zh: 師行大獲、雲頂、長寧、苦竹諸寨，長驅而前，至釣魚山，崖壁巉峭，惟一徑可登，恃險阻未即降。

translations.literal: The army marched through the stockades of Dahuo, Yunding, Changning, and Kuzhu, drove straight forward to Diaoyu Mountain; the cliffs were sheer and only one path could be climbed; relying on the terrain they did not immediately surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The army took the stockades of Dahuo, Yunding, Changning, and Kuzhu and pressed on to Diaoyu Mountain, whose cliffs allowed only a single path; the defenders held the heights and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 帝命攻之，文蔚以次往攻，迺激厲將士，挾雲梯，冒飛石，履崎嶇以登，直抵其寨苦戰，頃之，兵士被傷，迺還。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the attack; Wenwei went in turn to assault, then roused the officers and men, took scaling ladders, braved flying stones, climbed the rugged heights, reached their stockade and fought bitterly; in a short while the soldiers were wounded and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to attack, Wenwei roused his men, raised scaling ladders, braved stones on the steep path, and fought at the stockade until his troops were wounded and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝親見之，加以賞賚。

translations.literal: The emperor saw this in person and bestowed rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor witnessed it and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，世祖置武衛軍，文蔚以鄧兵入為千戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong Kublai established the Martial Guard Army; Wenwei entered it as chiliarch with his Deng troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong (1261) Kublai formed the Martial Guard Army, and Wenwei entered as chiliarch with his Deng troops.

sentences.zh: 帝北狩，留屯上都。

translations.literal: When the emperor hunted north he remained garrisoned at Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went north on campaign Wenwei remained at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 三年，李璮反，據濟南，文蔚以麾下軍圍其南面，春秋力戰，城破璮誅，奏功還。

translations.literal: In the third year Li Tan rebelled and held Jinan; Wenwei with his troops besieged the south face, fought through spring and autumn with all his strength; when the city fell Tan was executed; he reported merit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1262) Li Tan rebelled at Jinan; Wenwei besieged the south gate, fought through the seasons, and when the city fell returned to report his merit.

sentences.zh: 至元五年七月十七日，以疾卒于上都之炭山。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day of the seventh month of the fifth year of Zhiyuan he died of illness at Tanshan near Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, fifth year of Zhiyuan (1268), he died of illness at Tanshan near Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 弟文忠，時為樞密僉院，乞護喪南還，帝甚憫之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wenzhong was then vice-director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; he begged to escort the coffin south; the emperor was deeply moved with pity.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Wenzhong, then vice-director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, begged to escort the coffin south; the emperor was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 泰定中，贈明威將軍、僉右衛使司事、上騎都尉、隴西郡伯。

translations.literal: In the Taiding reign he was posthumously made General of Illustrious Might, vice-director of the Right Guard, Chief Commandant of Cavalry of the Upper Third Rank, and Baron of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taiding he was posthumously made General of Illustrious Might, vice-director of the Right Guard, Chief Commandant of Cavalry, and Baron of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 文用字彥材，俊之第三子也。

translations.literal: Wenyong, courtesy name Yancai, was Jun's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong, whose courtesy name was Yancai, was Jun's third son.

sentences.zh: 生十歲，父死，長兄文炳教諸弟有法。

translations.literal: At ten his father died; his eldest brother Wenbing taught the younger brothers with proper method.
translations.idiomatic: His father died when he was ten; his eldest brother Wenbing reared the younger brothers with discipline.

sentences.zh: 文用學問早成，弱冠試詞賦中選。

translations.literal: Wenyong's learning matured early; in his weak-capped years he passed the poetry-and-prose examination.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong's scholarship ripened early; in his youth he passed the poetry-and-prose examination.

sentences.zh: 時以真定藁城奉莊聖太后湯沐，庚戌，太后命擇邑中子弟來上，文用始從文炳謁太后于和林城。

translations.literal: At that time Gaocheng in Zhending was held as the empress dowager's bath fief; in gengxu the empress dowager ordered selection of youths from the district to come to court; Wenyong first followed Wenbing to pay respects to the empress dowager at Helin.
translations.idiomatic: Gaocheng in Zhending was then the bath fief of Empress Dowager Zhuangsheng; in gengxu (1250) she ordered youths from the district to court, and Wenyong first accompanied Wenbing to greet her at Helin.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛藩，命文用主文書，講說帳中，常見許重。

translations.literal: Kublai was still in his princely domain and ordered Wenyong to manage documents and lecture in his tent; he was often shown special esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai, still prince, put Wenyong in charge of documents and lectured with him in his tent, often showing him marked favor.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，世祖受命憲宗自河西征雲南大理。

translations.literal: In guichou Kublai received Möngke Khan's commission to campaign from Hexi against Dali in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In guichou (1253) Kublai received Möngke's commission to march from Hexi against Dali in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 文用與弟文忠從軍，督糧械，贊軍務。

translations.literal: Wenyong and his younger brother Wenzhong followed the army, supervised grain and equipment, and assisted in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong and his brother Wenzhong followed the campaign, overseeing grain and matériel and advising on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，世祖令授皇子經，是為北平王、雲南王也。

translations.literal: In dingsi Kublai ordered him to instruct the princes in the classics—these were the Prince of Beiping and the Prince of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In dingsi (1257) Kublai ordered him to teach the princes—the future Prince of Beiping and Prince of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 又命召遺老竇默、姚樞、李俊民、李冶、魏璠於四方。

translations.literal: He also ordered summons to the surviving elders Dou Mo, Yao Shu, Li Junmin, Li Ye, and Wei Fan from the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered summons to the surviving scholars Dou Mo, Yao Shu, Li Junmin, Li Ye, and Wei Fan from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 己未，伐宋，文用發沿邊蒙古、漢人諸軍，理軍需。

translations.literal: In jiwei, attacking Song, Wenyong mobilized Mongol and Han troops along the frontier and arranged military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei (1259), on the Song campaign, Wenyong mobilized Mongol and Han troops along the frontier and arranged supplies.

sentences.zh: 將攻鄂州，宋賈似道、呂文德將兵來拒，水陸軍容甚盛。

translations.literal: About to attack Ezhou, Song's Jia Sidao and Lü Wende led troops to resist; their land and water forces were very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared to attack Ezhou, Jia Sidao and Lü Wende of Song met them with a formidable land and river force.

sentences.zh: 九月，世祖臨江閱戰，文炳求先進戰，文用與文忠固請偕行，世祖親料甲冑，擇大艦授之，大破宋師。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Kublai reviewed the battle at the river; Wenbing asked to fight in the van; Wenyong and Wenzhong firmly begged to go with him; the emperor personally fitted their armor, chose great ships for them, and they routed the Song army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Kublai reviewed the battle from the river; Wenbing asked to lead the assault; Wenyong and Wenzhong begged to go with him; the emperor armed them himself, gave them the largest ships, and they shattered the Song force.

sentences.zh: 至元改元，召為西夏中興等路行省郎中。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Zhiyuan he was summoned as director of the Secretariat of the Xingzhong and neighboring circuits of Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhiyuan began he was summoned as director of the Secretariat of the Xingzhong and neighboring circuits of Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 中興自渾都海之亂，民間相恐動，竄匿山谷。

translations.literal: Since the turmoil of Hunduhai, the people had been mutually alarmed and hid in mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Since Hunduhai's rebellion the people had fled in panic to the mountains.

sentences.zh: 文用至，鎮之以靜，乃為書置通衢諭之，民乃安。

translations.literal: When Wenyong arrived he calmed them with quiet authority, then set up proclamations on the public roads to instruct them, and the people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong restored calm, posted proclamations on the highways, and the people settled.

sentences.zh: 始開唐來、漢延、秦家等渠，墾中興、西涼、甘、肅、瓜、沙等州之土為水田若干，於是民之歸者戶四五萬，悉授田種，頒農具；

translations.literal: He first opened the canals of Tanglai, Hanyan, and Qinjia and reclaimed land in Xingzhong, Xiliang, Gan, Su, Gua, Sha, and other prefectures as paddy fields; thus those who returned numbered forty or fifty thousand households, and all were given fields, seed, and farm tools;
translations.idiomatic: He opened the Tanglai, Hanyan, and Qinjia canals and reclaimed paddy in Xingzhong, Xiliang, Gan, Su, Gua, Sha, and neighboring prefectures; forty or fifty thousand households returned and received land, seed, and tools;

sentences.zh: 更造舟置黃河中，受諸部落及潰叛之來降者。

translations.literal: he also built boats and placed them on the Yellow River to receive tribes and those who came over from defeat and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: he built boats on the Yellow River to receive tribesmen and those who surrendered after defeat or rebellion.

sentences.zh: 時諸王只必鐵木兒鎮西方，其下縱橫，需索無筭，省臣不能支，文用坐幕府，輒面折以法。

translations.literal: At that time the prince Zhibie Timur was stationed in the west; his subordinates ran rampant, their demands beyond counting; the provincial officials could not sustain it; Dong Wenyong sat in the commandery staff and repeatedly rebuked them face to face according to the law.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Zhibie Timur held the west; his men ran wild with endless demands the provincial officials could not meet. Dong Wenyong, serving on the commandery staff, repeatedly confronted them and checked them by law.

sentences.zh: 其徒積忿，譖文用於王，王怒，召文用，使左右雜問之，意叵測。

translations.literal: His followers nursed resentment and slandered Dong Wenyong to the prince; the prince grew angry, summoned Dong Wenyong, and had his attendants question him on various charges—their intent impossible to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: His followers nursed their grievances and denounced Dong Wenyong to the prince. The prince flew into a rage, summoned him, and had his attendants cross-question him on all manner of charges—no one could tell what they meant to do.

sentences.zh: 文用曰：「我天子命吏，非汝等所當問，請得與天子所遣為王傅者辨之。」

translations.literal: Dong Wenyong said: "I am an official appointed by the Son of Heaven; it is not for you to question me—I ask to argue the matter with the tutor the Son of Heaven dispatched to serve the prince."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenyong said, "I am an officer appointed by the Son of Heaven—not someone you may question. Let me settle this with the tutor the emperor sent to serve the prince."

sentences.zh: 王即遣其傅訊文用。

translations.literal: The prince at once sent his tutor to examine Dong Wenyong.
translations.idiomatic: The prince immediately sent his tutor to question Dong Wenyong.

sentences.zh: 其傅中朝舊臣，不肯順王意。

translations.literal: The tutor was a former official of the central court and would not go along with the prince's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: The tutor was a veteran official of the central court and refused to bend to the prince's wishes.

sentences.zh: 文用謂之曰：「我漢人，生死不足計。

translations.literal: Dong Wenyong said to him: "I am a Han Chinese; life and death are not worth reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenyong told him, "I am a Han man—life and death are nothing to me.

sentences.zh: 所恨者，仁慈寬厚如王，以重戚鎮遠方，而其下毒虐百姓，凌暴官府，傷王威名，於事體不便。」

translations.literal: What I regret is that a prince as benevolent and broad-minded as this, a close kinsman holding distant territory, has subordinates who brutally abuse the people and bully the officials, harming the prince's reputation and making matters altogether inconvenient."
translations.idiomatic: What I regret is that a prince as benevolent and magnanimous as you, a royal kinsman holding distant territory, should have subordinates who brutalize the people and bully the officials—damaging your standing and making everything harder."

sentences.zh: 因歷指其不法者數十事，其傅驚起，去白王，王即召文用謝之曰：「非郎中，我殆不知。

translations.literal: Thereupon he enumerated dozens of their unlawful acts; the tutor started up in alarm, went to inform the prince, and the prince immediately summoned Dong Wenyong and apologized: "Had it not been for you, Langzhong, I would have been close to not knowing.
translations.idiomatic: He then listed dozens of their illegal acts one by one. The tutor rose in alarm, went to tell the prince, and the prince at once summoned Dong Wenyong and apologized: "But for you, Langzhong, I would never have known.

sentences.zh: 郎中持此心事朝廷，宜勿怠。」

translations.literal: Langzhong, hold this intent in service of the court—see that you do not slacken."
translations.idiomatic: Langzhong, keep this loyalty in mind for the court's sake—and do not slacken."

sentences.zh: 自是譖不行而省府事頗立。

translations.literal: From then on slander did not prevail and the provincial administration was largely established.
translations.idiomatic: After that slander no longer carried the day, and the provincial administration took solid shape.

sentences.zh: 二年，入奏經略事宜還，以上旨行之，中興遂定。

translations.literal: In the second year he went in to report on frontier strategy and returned; carrying out the emperor's intent, the Xingzhong region was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he went to court to report on frontier strategy and returned; acting on the emperor's orders, he settled the Xingzhong region.

sentences.zh: 八年，立司農司，授山東東西道巡行勸農使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Directorate of Agriculture was established, and he was appointed itinerant Agriculture Commissioner for the Eastern and Western Circuits of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Directorate of Agriculture was established, and he was made itinerant commissioner to promote farming in the Eastern and Western Shandong circuits.

sentences.zh: 山東自更叛亂，野多曠土，文用巡行勸勵，無間幽僻。

translations.literal: Since repeated rebellions in Shandong the countryside had much untilled land; Dong Wenyong toured to encourage farming, sparing neither remote nor secluded places.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated rebellions Shandong had much untilled land; Dong Wenyong toured the circuit to encourage farming, leaving no remote corner untouched.

sentences.zh: 入登州境，見其墾辟有方，以郡守移剌某為能，作詩表異之。

translations.literal: Entering the territory of Dengzhou, he saw its land opened and cultivated in good order; deeming the prefect Yelü so-and-so capable, he composed a poem to mark him out for distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Dengzhou, he saw land well cleared and planted; judging the prefect Yelü capable, he wrote a poem to honor him.

sentences.zh: 於是列郡咸勸，地利畢興，五年之間，政績為天下勸農使之最。

translations.literal: Thereupon every prefecture was encouraged; agricultural potential was fully developed; within five years his administrative record ranked first among all itinerant agriculture commissioners in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Every prefecture followed suit, and the land's potential was fully realized; within five years his record ranked first among all agriculture commissioners in the realm.

sentences.zh: 十二年，丞相安童奏文用為工部侍郎，代紇石里。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Chancellor An Tong memorialized to appoint Dong Wenyong Vice Minister of Works, replacing Hesiheri.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Chancellor An Tong recommended Dong Wenyong as Vice Minister of Works to replace Hesiheri.

sentences.zh: 紇石里，阿合馬私人也。

translations.literal: Hesiheri was Ahmad's personal man.
translations.idiomatic: Hesiheri was Ahmad's own man.

sentences.zh: 其徒既讒間安童罷相，即使鷹監奏曰：「自紇石里去，工部侍郎不給鷹食，鷹且瘦死。」

translations.literal: Once his faction had slandered An Tong into removal from the chancellorship, they had the hawk supervisor memorialize: "Since Hesiheri left, the Vice Minister of Works has not supplied hawk food—the hawks will soon starve to death."
translations.idiomatic: Once his faction had slandered An Tong out of office, they had the hawk keeper report: "Since Hesiheri left, the Vice Minister of Works has not fed the hawks—they will soon starve."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，促召治之，因急捕文用入見，帝望見曰：「董文用乃為爾治鷹食者耶！」

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and urgently summoned him for punishment; they hastily seized Dong Wenyong and brought him before the emperor, who saw him at a glance and said: "Is Dong Wenyong really the one who is supposed to feed your hawks!"
translations.idiomatic: Kublai flew into a rage and ordered him seized at once; they hurried Dong Wenyong in to audience. The emperor took one look and said, "Is Dong Wenyong really the man who feeds your hawks!"

sentences.zh: 置不問，別令取給有司。

translations.literal: He dismissed the matter and separately ordered the appropriate offices to provide the supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the matter and ordered the proper offices to supply the hawks instead.

sentences.zh: 十三年，出文用為衛輝路緫管，佩金虎符。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Dong Wenyong was sent out as Commissioner of Weihui Circuit, bearing the golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Dong Wenyong was posted as commissioner of Weihui Circuit, bearing the golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 郡當衝要，民為兵者十之九，餘皆單弱貧病，不堪力役。

translations.literal: The prefecture lay at a strategic crossing; nine-tenths of the people were soldiers; the rest were all lone, weak, poor, or sick and could not bear corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture stood at a strategic crossroads; nine in ten of the people were soldiers, and the rest were solitary, weak, poor, or sick—unable to bear corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 會初得江南，圖籍、金玉、財帛之運，日夜不絕于道，警衛輸輓，日役數千夫。

translations.literal: Just then the newly taken Jiangnan was sending maps, registers, gold and jade, and goods and silks—the traffic on the roads day and night unceasing; guard escorts and transport crews requisitioned thousands of laborers daily.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the newly conquered Jiangnan was sending maps, registers, gold, jade, and treasure along the roads without pause day or night; escorts and transport crews pressed thousands of men into service each day.

sentences.zh: 文用憂之曰：「吾民弊矣，而又重妨耕作，殆不可。」

translations.literal: Dong Wenyong worried and said: "Our people are exhausted, and this again seriously hinders farming—it can hardly stand."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenyong worried and said, "Our people are worn out, and this again badly interferes with farming—it cannot go on."

sentences.zh: 乃從轉運主者言：「州縣吏卒，足以備用，不必重煩吾民也。」

translations.literal: He therefore followed the transport commissioner in saying: "The clerks and soldiers of the prefectures and counties are enough for our needs; there is no need again to heavily burden our people."
translations.idiomatic: He therefore told the transport commissioner, "The clerks and soldiers of the prefectures and counties are enough—we need not burden our people again."

sentences.zh: 主者曰：「汝言誠然，萬一有不虞，則罪將誰歸！」

translations.literal: The commissioner said: "What you say is indeed so—but if something unforeseen should happen, to whom would the blame fall!"
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner said, "What you say is true—but if anything goes wrong, who will bear the blame!"

sentences.zh: 文用即手書具官姓名保任之。

translations.literal: Dong Wenyong at once wrote by hand the names and offices of all who would guarantee it.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenyong immediately wrote out by hand the names and offices of every official who would guarantee the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 民得以時耕，而運事亦不廢。

translations.literal: The people were able to farm on schedule, and transport affairs were not disrupted either.
translations.idiomatic: The people could farm on time, and transport was not disrupted.

sentences.zh: 諸郡運江淮粟于京師，衛當運十五萬石，文用曰：「民籍可役者無幾，且江淮風水，舟不能以時至，而先為期會，是未運而民已困矣。」

translations.literal: The various prefectures transported grain from the Jianghuai region to the capital; Weihui was charged with transport of 150,000 piculs; Dong Wenyong said: "Those on the registers fit for corvée are few; moreover, wind and water on the Jianghuai route mean boats cannot arrive on time—yet deadlines are set in advance, so the people are exhausted before transport even begins."
translations.idiomatic: Every prefecture was shipping Jianghuai grain to the capital; Weihui was assigned 150,000 piculs. Dong Wenyong said, "Few on the registers can be pressed into service; moreover, wind and water on the Jianghuai route keep boats from arriving on schedule—yet deadlines are fixed in advance, so the people are exhausted before a single load moves."

sentences.zh: 乃集旁郡通議，立驛置法，民力以舒。

translations.literal: He then convened neighboring prefectures for joint deliberation, established relay-station regulations, and the people's labor burden was eased.
translations.idiomatic: He then convened neighboring prefectures for joint discussion, established relay-station rules, and eased the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 十四年，詣汴漕司言事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he went to the Bianliang Grain Transport Office to report on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he went to the Bianliang grain transport office to report on affairs.

sentences.zh: 適漕司議通沁水北東合流御河以便漕者，文用曰：「衛為郡，地最下，大雨時行，沁水輒溢出百十里間；

translations.literal: Just then the transport office was debating opening the Qin River so its northward and eastward flows would merge with the Imperial Canal to ease transport; Dong Wenyong said: "Weihui as a prefecture occupies the lowest ground; when heavy rains come from time to time, the Qin River always overflows across a hundred or more li;
translations.idiomatic: Just then the transport office was debating diverting the Qin River north and east to join the Imperial Canal for easier shipping. Dong Wenyong said, "Weihui is the lowest ground in the region; when heavy rains come, the Qin River always overflows for a hundred li or more;

sentences.zh: 雨更甚，水不得達于河，即浸淫及衛，今又引之使來，豈惟無衛，將無大名、長蘆矣。」

translations.literal: when the rains grow heavier, the water cannot reach the River and at once spreads and invades Weihui—now you would also draw it here; will Weihui not be the only land lost? Daming and Changlu will soon be gone as well."
translations.idiomatic: when the rains grow worse the water cannot reach the Yellow River and spreads into Weihui—now you would also draw it here; Weihui will not be the only place lost—Daming and Changlu will go too."

sentences.zh: 會朝廷遣使相地形，上言：「衛州城中浮屠最高者，纔與沁水平，勢不可開也。」

translations.literal: Just then the court dispatched envoys to survey the terrain; they submitted: "The tallest pagoda in Weizhou city is only level with the Qin River—the terrain makes opening impossible."
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent envoys to survey the terrain; they reported, "The tallest pagoda in Weizhou city is only level with the Qin River—the land makes opening the channel impossible."

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十六年，受代歸田里，茅茨數椽，僅避風雨，讀書賦詩，怡然燕居。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, at the end of his term he returned to his fields—several thatched beams barely keeping off wind and rain—reading books and composing poetry, dwelling at ease in pleasant retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, when his term ended, he returned home to a few thatched beams barely sheltering him from wind and rain, reading and writing poetry in contented retirement.

sentences.zh: 裕宗在東宮，數為臺臣言：「董文用勳舊忠良，何以不見用！」

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhaozong was in the Eastern Palace and repeatedly told censorate officials: "Dong Wenyong is a meritorious old servant and loyal—why is he not being employed!"
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhaozong, in the Eastern Palace, repeatedly told censorate officials, "Dong Wenyong is a meritorious veteran and a loyal man—why is he not being used!"

sentences.zh: 十八年，臺臣奏起文用為山北遼東道提刑按察使，不赴。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year censorate officials memorialized to recall Dong Wenyong as Judicial Commissioner of the Shanbei Liaodong Circuit; he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the censorate recommended recalling Dong Wenyong as judicial commissioner of the Shanbei Liaodong circuit; he did not go.

sentences.zh: 十九年，朝廷選用舊臣，召文用為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the court selected former officials and summoned Dong Wenyong as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the court drew on former officials and summoned Dong Wenyong as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 自是朝廷有大議，未嘗不與聞。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever the court debated great affairs, he was always consulted.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was always consulted whenever the court debated major affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十年，江淮省臣有欲專肆而忌廉察官，建議行臺隸行省，狀上，集朝臣議之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year provincial officials of Jianghuai, who wished to act without restraint and resented the supervisory censors, proposed subordinating the regional censorate to the provincial administration; the memorial went up, and court officials were assembled to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Jianghuai provincial officials, wanting free rein and resenting the supervisory censors, proposed placing the regional censorate under the provincial administration; the memorial went up and court officials were assembled to debate it.

sentences.zh: 文用議曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Dong Wenyong argued: "This cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenyong argued, "That cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 御史臺，譬之卧虎，雖未噬人，人猶畏其為虎也。

translations.literal: The Censorate is like a tiger lying down—though it has not yet bitten anyone, people still fear it as a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate is like a crouching tiger—though it has not yet bitten anyone, people still fear it as a tiger.

sentences.zh: 今虛名僅存，紀綱猶不振，一旦摧抑之，則風采薾然，無可復望者矣。

translations.literal: Now only the empty name remains, and discipline is still not restored—once it is crushed and suppressed, its authority will wilt entirely and nothing can be hoped for again.
translations.idiomatic: Today only the name survives, and discipline is still weak—crush it once and its authority will wither, with nothing left to hope for.

sentences.zh: 昔阿合馬用事時，商賈賤役，皆行賄入官，及事敗，欲盡去其人，廷議以為不可，使阿合馬售私恩，而朝廷驟斂怨也。

translations.literal: In the past when Ahmad held power, merchants and menials all gained office through bribery; when the affair broke, there was a wish to remove them all, but court deliberation held this impossible—let Ahmad sell his private favors while the court suddenly gathered resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Ahmad was in power, merchants and menials all bought their way into office; when the scandal broke, some wanted to purge them all, but court debate held that impossible—it would let Ahmad dispense private favors while the court suddenly collected hatred.

sentences.zh: 乃使按察司劾去其不可者，然後吏有所憚，民有所赴訴。

translations.literal: Instead they had the surveillance commissions impeach those who were unfit; only then did officials feel awe and the people have somewhere to bring grievances.
translations.idiomatic: Instead they had the surveillance commissions impeach the unfit; only then did officials feel restraint and the people have somewhere to bring grievances.

sentences.zh: 則是按察司者，國家當飭勵之，不可摧抑也。」

translations.literal: The surveillance commissions, then, the state should encourage and invigorate—they must not be suppressed."
translations.idiomatic: The surveillance commissions are what the state should strengthen—not suppress."

sentences.zh: 悉從文用議。

translations.literal: All his recommendations were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted Dong Wenyong's position entirely.

sentences.zh: 轉禮部尚書，遷翰林、集賢二院學士，知祕書監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites, promoted to academician of the Hanlin and Jixian Academies, and made Director of the Directorate of Archives.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Rites, promoted to academician of the Hanlin and Jixian academies, and made director of the Directorate of Archives.

sentences.zh: 時中書右丞盧世榮，以貨利得幸權要為貴官，陰結貪刻之黨，以錙銖掊克為功，乃建議曰：「我立法治財，視常歲當倍增，而民不擾也。」

translations.literal: At that time Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat Lu Shirong, having won favor through profits and attached himself to the powerful as a high official, secretly joined a faction of greedy and harsh men and made squeezing every mote of gain his achievement; he proposed: "If I establish laws to govern wealth, compared with an ordinary year revenue should double, yet the people will not be disturbed."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Right Vice Minister Lu Shirong, having won favor through profit and risen by attaching himself to the powerful, secretly gathered a faction of greedy and harsh men and made squeezing every coin his achievement. He proposed, "If I establish laws to govern revenue, it should double an ordinary year's take—and the people will not be disturbed."

sentences.zh: 詔下會議，人無敢言者。

translations.literal: An edict went down for joint discussion, and no one dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went down for joint discussion, and no one dared speak up.

sentences.zh: 文用陽問曰：「此錢取於右丞之家耶？

translations.literal: Dong Wenyong asked as if casually: "Is this money to be taken from the Vice Minister's own household?
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenyong asked as if casually, "Is this money to come from the Vice Minister's own household?

sentences.zh: 將取之於民耶？

translations.literal: Or taken from the people?
translations.idiomatic: Or from the people?

sentences.zh: 取於右丞之家，則不敢知；

translations.literal: Taken from the Vice Minister's household—then I dare not inquire further;
translations.idiomatic: If it comes from the Vice Minister's household, I dare not inquire further;

sentences.zh: 若取諸民，則有說矣。

translations.literal: but if taken from the people, then I have something to say.
translations.idiomatic: but if it comes from the people, then I have something to say.

sentences.zh: 牧羊者，歲嘗兩剪其毛，今牧人日剪其毛而獻之，則主者固悅其得毛之多矣，然而羊無以避寒熱，即死且盡，毛又可得哉！

translations.literal: One who raises sheep shears their wool twice a year; now suppose the herdsman shears wool daily and presents it—then the owner will surely be pleased at receiving so much wool; yet the sheep have no way to ward off cold and heat and will soon all die—then what wool can be had!
translations.idiomatic: A shepherd shears wool twice a year; now suppose the herdsman shears wool every day and presents it—the owner will be pleased at getting so much wool, yet the sheep cannot ward off cold and heat and will soon all die—then what wool will there be!

sentences.zh: 民財亦有限，取之以時，猶懼其傷殘也。

translations.literal: The people's wealth, too, is limited; even when taken in season, one still fears injury and depletion.
translations.idiomatic: The people's wealth is limited too; even when taken in season one still fears depletion.

sentences.zh: 今盡刻剝無遺，猶有百姓乎！」

translations.literal: Now you would scrape and strip everything without remainder—will there still be any common people!"
translations.idiomatic: Now you would scrape them clean—will there still be any common people left!"

sentences.zh: 世榮不能對。

translations.literal: Shirong could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shirong had no reply.

sentences.zh: 丞相安童謂坐中曰：「董尚書真不虛食俸祿者。」

translations.literal: Chancellor An Tong said to those seated: "Minister Dong truly does not eat his salary for nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor An Tong said to those present, "Minister Dong truly does not eat his salary for nothing."

sentences.zh: 議者出，皆謝文用曰：「君以一言，折聚斂之臣，而厚邦本，真仁人之言哉。」

translations.literal: When the deliberators left, they all thanked Dong Wenyong: "With a single word you have rebutted the minister of exactions and strengthened the foundation of the state—a true man's words indeed."
translations.idiomatic: When the deliberators left, they all thanked Dong Wenyong: "With one sentence you have rebutted the minister of exactions and strengthened the state's foundation—words worthy of a true man."

sentences.zh: 世榮竟以是得罪。

translations.literal: Shirong ultimately fell from grace on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shirong ultimately fell from power on this account.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，拜江淮行中書省參知政事，文用力辭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Vice Administrator of the Jianghuai Branch Secretariat; Dong Wenyong strongly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was appointed vice administrator of the Jianghuai branch secretariat; Dong Wenyong firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿家世非他人比。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your family and generation are not like others.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "Your family and generation are not like others.

sentences.zh: 朕所以任卿者，不在錢穀細務也，卿當察其大者，事有不便，但言之。」

translations.literal: The reason I appoint you is not for grain and coin in petty detail—you should examine the larger matters; where anything is inconvenient, speak out."
translations.idiomatic: I appoint you not for grain and coin in petty detail—you should watch the larger matters; where anything is wrong, speak out."

sentences.zh: 文用遂行。

translations.literal: Dong Wenyong then took up the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenyong then took up the post.

sentences.zh: 行省長官者，素貴多傲，同列莫敢仰視，跪起稟白，如小吏事上官。

translations.literal: The chief administrators of branch secretariats had long been high-born and mostly arrogant; colleagues dared not look up at them—kneeling, rising, reporting as petty clerks serving superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Branch secretariat chiefs had long been high-born and mostly arrogant; colleagues dared not meet their eyes—kneeling, rising, and reporting like petty clerks before a superior.

sentences.zh: 文用至，則坐堂上，侃侃與論是非可否，無所遷就，雖數忤之，不顧也。

translations.literal: When Dong Wenyong arrived, he sat in the hall and frankly debated right and wrong with them without yielding, though he often offended them, paying no heed.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Wenyong arrived, he sat in the hall and spoke plainly on right and wrong without yielding, often offending them—and paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 有以帝命建佛塔於宋故宮者，有司奉行甚急，天大雨雪，入山伐木，死者數百人，猶欲併建大寺。

translations.literal: By imperial command a Buddhist pagoda was to be built on the site of the former Song palace; the responsible offices carried it out with great urgency—amid heavy rain and snow they entered the mountains to fell timber; hundreds died, yet they still wished to build a great monastery together with it.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command a Buddhist pagoda was to be built on the site of the former Song palace; the offices rushed to obey—in heavy rain and snow they went into the mountains to cut timber, and hundreds died, yet they still wanted to build a great monastery as well.

sentences.zh: 文用謂其人曰：「非時役民，民不堪矣，少徐之如何？」

translations.literal: Dong Wenyong said to the man in charge: "To press the people into service out of season—they cannot bear it—why not slow down a little?"
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenyong told the man in charge, "Pressing the people into service out of season—they cannot bear it—why not slow down a little?"

sentences.zh: 長官者曰：「參政奈何格上命耶？」

translations.literal: The chief administrator said: "How can the Vice Administrator resist the emperor's command?"
translations.idiomatic: The chief administrator said, "How can the Vice Administrator resist the emperor's command?"

sentences.zh: 文用曰：「非敢格上命，今日之困民力而失民心者，豈上意耶！」

translations.literal: Dong Wenyong said: "I do not dare resist the emperor's command—but to exhaust the people's strength today and lose the people's hearts, is that the emperor's intent!"
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenyong said, "I do not dare resist the emperor's command—but to exhaust the people's strength and lose their hearts today—is that the emperor's intent!"

sentences.zh: 其人意沮，遂稍寬其期。

translations.literal: The man lost heart, and the deadline was slightly relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: The man lost heart, and the deadline was eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，朝廷將用兵海東，徵斂益急，有司大為奸利。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the court was preparing to use troops in the eastern sea; exactions grew ever sharper, and the offices greatly profited by fraud.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year the court was preparing to use troops in the eastern sea; exactions grew ever harsher, and the offices profited greatly by fraud.

sentences.zh: 文用請入奏事，大略言：「疲國家可寶之民力，取僻陋無用之小邦。」

translations.literal: Dong Wenyong requested audience to report, stating in outline: "To exhaust the state's precious manpower in order to take a remote, useless petty realm."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenyong requested audience and argued in outline, "To exhaust the state's precious manpower for a remote, useless petty realm."

sentences.zh: 列其條目甚悉。

translations.literal: He listed the points in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: He listed the points in full detail.

sentences.zh: 言上，事遂罷。

translations.literal: When his words reached the throne, the affair was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When his words reached the throne, the campaign was dropped.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 文用曰：「中丞不當理細務，吾當先舉賢才。」

translations.literal: Dong Wenyong said: "The vice censor-in-chief ought not handle petty affairs—I should first recommend worthy talent."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenyong said, "The vice censor-in-chief should not handle petty affairs—I should first recommend worthy talent."

sentences.zh: 乃舉胡祗遹、王惲、雷膺、荊幼紀、許楫、孔從道十餘人為按察使，徐琰、魏初為行臺中丞，當時以為極選。

translations.literal: He then recommended Hu Zhiyuan, Wang Yun, Lei Ying, Jing Youji, Xu Ji, Kong Congdao, and more than ten others as surveillance commissioners, and Xu Yan and Wei Chu as regional censorate vice commissioners—regarded at the time as the finest selections.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended Hu Zhiyuan, Wang Yun, Lei Ying, Jing Youji, Xu Ji, Kong Congdao, and more than ten others as surveillance commissioners, and Xu Yan and Wei Chu as regional censorate vice commissioners—regarded at the time as the finest appointments.

sentences.zh: 方是時，桑哥當國，恩寵方盛，自近戚貴人見之，皆屏息遜避，無敢誰何。

translations.literal: At that time Sangge held the state; imperial favor was at its height—even close kinsmen and nobles, on seeing him, held their breath and gave way, daring not challenge him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sangge held the state and imperial favor was at its height—even close kinsmen and nobles held their breath and gave way on seeing him, daring not challenge him.

sentences.zh: 文用以舊臣任中丞，獨不附之。

translations.literal: Dong Wenyong, an old servant appointed vice censor-in-chief, alone would not attach himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenyong, an old servant appointed vice censor-in-chief, alone would not attach himself to Sangge.

sentences.zh: 桑哥令人風文用頌己功於帝前，文用不荅。

translations.literal: Sangge had someone hint that Dong Wenyong should praise his achievements before the emperor; Dong Wenyong did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Sangge had someone hint that Dong Wenyong should praise his achievements before the emperor; Dong Wenyong did not respond.

sentences.zh: 桑哥又自謂文用曰：「百司皆具食於丞相府矣。」

translations.literal: Sangge also said to Dong Wenyong himself: "Every office now takes its meals at the chancellor's mansion."
translations.idiomatic: Sangge also told Dong Wenyong himself, "Every office now takes its meals at the chancellor's mansion."

sentences.zh: 文用又不荅。

translations.literal: Dong Wenyong again did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenyong again did not respond.

sentences.zh: 會朔方軍興，糧糗粗備，而誅求愈急，文用謂桑哥曰：「民急矣。

translations.literal: When the ShuoFang campaign began, grain and fodder were roughly prepared, yet demands grew ever harsher; Dong Wenyong said to Sangge: "The people are at the breaking point.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shuofang campaign began, grain and fodder were roughly in place, yet exactions grew ever harsher; Dong Wenyong told Sangge, "The people are at the breaking point.

sentences.zh: 外難未解而內伐其根本，丞相宜思之。」

translations.literal: External hardship is not yet resolved, yet you are cutting at the roots within—the Chancellor should consider this."
translations.idiomatic: External danger is not yet past, yet you are cutting at the roots within—Chancellor, you should think on this."

sentences.zh: 於是遠邇盜賊蜂起，文用持外郡所上盜賊之目，謂桑哥曰：「百姓豈不欲生養安樂哉！

translations.literal: Then bandits rose everywhere near and far; Dong Wenyong took the lists of bandits submitted by outer prefectures and said to Sangge: "Do the common people not wish to live, be nourished, and know peace!
translations.idiomatic: Then bandits rose everywhere near and far; Dong Wenyong took the lists of bandits submitted by outer prefectures and said to Sangge, "Do the common people not wish to live in peace and plenty!

sentences.zh: 急法暴斂使至此爾。

translations.literal: Harsh laws and violent exactions have brought them to this.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh laws and violent exactions have brought them to this.

sentences.zh: 御史臺所以救政事之不及，丞相當助之，不當抑之也。

translations.literal: The purpose of the Censorate is to remedy what governance cannot reach—the Chancellor should assist it, not suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate exists to remedy what governance cannot reach—the Chancellor should help it, not suppress it.

sentences.zh: 御史臺不得行，則民無所赴愬；

translations.literal: If the Censorate cannot act, the people have nowhere to bring grievances;
translations.idiomatic: If the Censorate cannot act, the people have nowhere to bring grievances;

sentences.zh: 民無所赴愬，而政日亂，將不止於臺事之不行也。」

translations.literal: with nowhere to bring grievances, government grows daily more chaotic—and it will not stop at the censorate's failure to act."
translations.idiomatic: with nowhere to bring grievances, government grows daily more chaotic—and it will not stop at the censorate's failure to act."

sentences.zh: 忤其意益深，乃摭拾臺事百端，文用日與辨論，不為屈。

translations.literal: This offended him all the more deeply; he then dredged up a hundred pretexts from censorate affairs, and Dong Wenyong debated them day after day without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: This offended him all the more; Sangge dredged up a hundred pretexts from censorate affairs, and Dong Wenyong debated them day after day without yielding.

sentences.zh: 於是具奏桑哥姦狀，詔報文用，語密而外人不知也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he fully memorialized Sangge's corrupt conduct; an edict replied to Dong Wenyong—its words secret, unknown to outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: He then fully memorialized Sangge's corrupt conduct; an edict replied to Dong Wenyong in secret words unknown to outsiders.

sentences.zh: 桑哥日誣譖文用于帝曰：「在朝惟董文用戇傲不聽令，沮撓尚書省，請痛治其罪。」

translations.literal: Day after day Sangge slandered Dong Wenyong before the emperor: "Among those at court only Dong Wenyong is obstinate and arrogant, disobedient to orders, obstructing the Secretariat—please severely punish his crime."
translations.idiomatic: Day after day Sangge slandered Dong Wenyong before the emperor: "Among those at court only Dong Wenyong is obstinate and arrogant, disobedient to orders, obstructing the Secretariat—please punish him severely."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「彼御史之職也，何罪之有！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That is the censor's duty—what crime is there!
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "That is the censor's duty—what crime is there!

sentences.zh: 且董文用端謹，朕所素知，汝善視之。」

translations.literal: Moreover Dong Wenyong is upright and careful, as I have long known—treat him well."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Dong Wenyong is upright and careful, as I have long known—treat him well."

sentences.zh: 遷大司農。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 時欲奪民田為屯田，文用固執不可。

translations.literal: At that time there was a plan to seize the people's fields for garrison colonies; Dong Wenyong firmly held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was a plan to seize the people's fields for garrison colonies; Dong Wenyong firmly held that this could not be done.

sentences.zh: 遷為翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Academician Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Academician Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，隆福太后在東宮，以文用舊臣，欲使文用授皇孫經，具奏上，以帝命命之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Empress Dowager Longfu was in the Eastern Palace; as Dong Wenyong was an old servant, she wished to have Dong Wenyong instruct the imperial grandson in the classics; she prepared a full memorial and submitted it upward, and by imperial command he was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (1290), Empress Dowager Longfu, resident in the Eastern Palace, wished to have Dong Wenyong—the old servant she knew—instruct the imperial grandson in the classics. She submitted a full memorial, and the emperor ordered the appointment.

sentences.zh: 文用每講說經旨，必附以朝廷故事，丁嚀譬喻，反復開悟，皇孫亦特加敬禮。

translations.literal: Whenever Dong Wenyong expounded the meaning of the classics, he always appended court precedents, admonished and illustrated with analogies, repeatedly enlightening him; the imperial grandson also showed him special respect and courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Dong Wenyong lectured on the classics, he wove in precedents from court history, repeating his points with homely analogies until the lesson took hold. The imperial grandson treated him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，帝命文用以其諸子入見，文用曰：「臣蒙國厚恩，死無以報，臣之子，何能為！」

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year the emperor ordered Dong Wenyong to bring his sons to audience; Dong Wenyong said: "Your subject has received the state's deep favor and has nothing with which to repay it even in death—what could my sons do!"
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year (1294) the emperor ordered Dong Wenyong to present his sons. Dong Wenyong said, "Your subject has received the state's great favor and has no way to repay it even by dying—what could my sons possibly do!"

sentences.zh: 命至再三，終不以見。

translations.literal: The command came again and again, yet in the end he would not bring them to audience.
translations.idiomatic: The command came again and again, yet he never brought them to audience.

sentences.zh: 是歲，世祖崩，成宗將即位上都，太后命文用從行。

translations.literal: That year Kublai passed away; Chengzong was about to ascend the throne at Shangdu; the empress dowager ordered Dong Wenyong to accompany the journey.
translations.idiomatic: That year Kublai died. As Chengzong was to be enthroned at Shangdu, the empress dowager ordered Dong Wenyong to accompany the party.

sentences.zh: 既即位，巡狩三不剌之地，文用曰：「先帝新棄天下，陛下巡狩，不以時還，無以慰安元元，宜趣還京師。

translations.literal: After his enthronement he hunted at Sanbula; Dong Wenyong said: "The late emperor has just left the realm; Your Majesty hunts and does not return in season—there is no way to soothe and reassure the masses; you should hasten back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After his enthronement Chengzong went hunting in Sanbula. Dong Wenyong said, "The late emperor has only just departed; if Your Majesty hunts abroad and does not return in good time, the people cannot be soothed. You should hurry back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 且臣聞人君猶北辰然，居其所而衆星拱之，不在勤遠略也。」

translations.literal: Moreover your subject has heard that the ruler is like the Pole Star—dwelling in his place the myriad stars encircle him; it lies not in being zealous for distant campaigns."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I have heard that the ruler is like the North Star: dwelling in his place, the myriad stars wheel around him. His strength is not in pressing far afield."

sentences.zh: 帝悟，即日可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and that same day approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his meaning and that same day approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 是行也，帝每召入帳中，問先朝故事，文用亦盛言先帝虛心納賢、開國經世之務，談說或至夜半。

translations.literal: On this journey the emperor often summoned him into the tent and asked about precedents of the previous reign; Dong Wenyong also spoke at length of the late emperor's open mind in receiving the worthy and affairs of founding the state and governing the age—talk sometimes lasted until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: On that journey the emperor often summoned him into his tent to ask about precedents of the previous reign. Dong Wenyong spoke at length of Kublai's openness to talent and of the founding work of the dynasty, and their talk sometimes ran until midnight.

sentences.zh: 文用自先帝時，每侍燕，與蒙古大臣同列，裕宗嘗就榻上賜酒，使毋下拜跪飲，皆異數也。

translations.literal: Since the late emperor's time, whenever Dong Wenyong attended banquets he sat in the same rank as Mongol ministers; Prince Yu once granted wine from the couch, ordering him not to descend, bow, or kneel to drink—all extraordinary honors.
translations.idiomatic: Since Kublai's day, whenever Dong Wenyong attended banquets he sat among the Mongol ministers as an equal. Prince Yu once offered wine from his couch and told him not to kneel and bow to drink—extraordinary favors all.

sentences.zh: 帝在東宮時，正旦受賀，於衆中見文用，召使前曰：「吾向見至尊，甚稱汝賢。」

translations.literal: When the emperor was in the Eastern Palace, on New Year's Day receiving congratulations, he saw Dong Wenyong in the crowd, summoned him forward and said: "When I last saw the Supreme One he greatly praised your worth."
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong was still in the Eastern Palace, at New Year's he saw Dong Wenyong in the crowd receiving congratulations and called him forward. "When I last saw His Majesty," he said, "he spoke highly of your worth."

sentences.zh: 輒親取酒飲之。

translations.literal: He then personally took wine and had him drink it.
translations.idiomatic: He personally poured wine and had him drink.

sentences.zh: 至是，眷賚益厚。

translations.literal: By this time gifts and favors grew ever fuller.
translations.idiomatic: By then imperial favor and gifts had grown even more generous.

sentences.zh: 是年，詔修先帝實錄，陞資德大夫、知制誥兼修國史。

translations.literal: That year an edict ordered compilation of the Veritable Record of the late emperor; he was promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Virtue, Drafting Edicts, and concurrently editing the National History.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict ordered the compilation of Kublai's Veritable Record, and Dong Wenyong was promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Virtue with charge of drafting edicts and editing the National History.

sentences.zh: 文用於祖宗世系功德、近戚將相家世勳績，皆記憶貫穿，史館有所考究質問，文用應之無遺失。

translations.literal: Dong Wenyong had thorough memory of the ancestral line's achievements, the meritorious records of close kin and generals and chancellors' lineages; whenever the historiographical office had inquiries to investigate and question, Dong Wenyong answered without omission.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenyong had thorough command of the imperial genealogy, the deeds of the forebears, and the honors of kinsmen and generals alike. When the historiographical office put questions to him, he answered without a single gap.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，上章請老，賜中統鈔萬貫以歸，官一子，鄉郡侍養。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; he was granted ten thousand strings of Zhongtong notes to return home, one son was given office, and he was to be cared for in his native district.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dade (1297) he memorialized for retirement. He was granted ten thousand strings of Zhongtong paper money to return home, one son received office, and he was to be maintained in his home district.

sentences.zh: 六月戊寅，以疾卒，年七十有四。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the sixth month, he died of illness, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin in the sixth month he died of illness, aged seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 子八人：士貞，士亨，士楷，士英，士昌，士恒，士廉，士方。

translations.literal: He had eight sons: Shizhen, Shiheng, Shikai, Shiying, Shichang, Shiheng, Shilian, and Shifang.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons: Shizhen, Shiheng, Shikai, Shiying, Shichang, Shiheng, Shilian, and Shifang.

sentences.zh: 贈銀青榮祿大夫、少保、趙國公，諡忠穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Silver-Girdled Grand Master for Glorious Blessings, Junior Guardian, Duke of Zhao; posthumous title Zhongmu ("Loyal and Solemn").
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of Silver-Girdled Grand Master for Glorious Blessings, Junior Guardian, and Duke of Zhao, with the posthumous title Zhongmu ("Loyal and Solemn").

sentences.zh: 文直字彥正，俊之第四子也。

translations.literal: Wenzhi, courtesy name Yanzhèng, was Jun's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenzhi, courtesy name Yanzhèng, was Jun's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 剛毅莊栗，簡言笑，通經史法律。

translations.literal: Firm, resolute, solemn, and restrained; sparing in speech and laughter; versed in the classics, history, and law.
translations.idiomatic: He was firm and solemn, sparing in speech and laughter, and versed in the classics, history, and law.

sentences.zh: 為藁城長官，佩金符。

translations.literal: He served as chief administrator of Gaocheng and wore the gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief magistrate of Gaocheng and wore a gold tally of authority.

sentences.zh: 初，兄文炳及季弟文忠，去事世祖，次文用亦在朝，俱有仰於家，而食者餘百口，文直勤儉，始終不替。

translations.literal: At first his elder brother Wenbing and youngest brother Wenzhong left to serve Kublai; next Wenyong also held court office—all had dependents at home, and those who ate numbered more than a hundred mouths; Wenzhi was diligent and frugal from start to finish without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Wenbing and youngest brother Wenzhong had left to serve Kublai; Wenyong too was at court. All looked to the household for support, and more than a hundred mouths depended on it. Wenzhi was diligent and frugal throughout without slackening.

sentences.zh: 內則養生送死之合禮，外則中表賓問之中度，奉上接下，一敬一愛，藹乎其睦也。
