translations.literal: Within, nurturing life and seeing off the dead accorded with ritual; without, relations and guests were received with proper measure; serving superiors and receiving inferiors—each with respect and each with love—harmonious and amiable indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Within the household he saw to life and death in proper ritual form; without, he received kin and guests with fitting measure. Toward superiors and inferiors alike he showed respect and affection—harmonious and warm.

sentences.zh: 性好施而甚仁，里閈或貧不自立，每陰濟其急，不使之知恩所從來。

translations.literal: By nature he loved giving and was deeply humane; when neighbors in the lanes were poor and could not support themselves, he secretly relieved their emergencies without letting them know whence the kindness came.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved to give and was deeply humane. Neighbors too poor to stand on their own he secretly helped in their emergencies, never letting them know the source of the kindness.

sentences.zh: 微至僮病，必手予粥藥。

translations.literal: Even down to a servant's illness, he always personally gave gruel and medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Even when a servant fell ill, he personally gave gruel and medicine.

sentences.zh: 或止之，曰：「不忍以其賤違吾愛心。」

translations.literal: When some tried to stop him, he said: "I cannot bear that because they are lowly I should turn aside my loving heart."
translations.idiomatic: When someone tried to stop him, he said, "I cannot let their low station turn aside my care."

sentences.zh: 及棄官，浮沉里社，任真適意，親賓過從，尊酒相勞。

translations.literal: When he abandoned office he drifted in village and community, following his true nature and pleasing himself; kin and guests came and went, offering wine in mutual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: After he left office he lived quietly in the village, following his own bent. Kin and guests visited, sharing wine and good cheer.

sentences.zh: 家門日以烜赫，己獨恬然，不見諸辭色。

translations.literal: The family gates grew daily more glorious, yet he alone remained tranquil, showing nothing of it in word or countenance.
translations.idiomatic: As the family's glory grew daily, he alone remained tranquil, giving no sign of it in word or face.

sentences.zh: 以病卒，年五十有二。

translations.literal: He died of illness, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness, aged fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 文忠字彥誠，俊第八子也。

translations.literal: Wenzhong, courtesy name Yancheng, was Jun's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenzhong, courtesy name Yancheng, was Jun's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 歲壬子，入侍世祖潛邸。

translations.literal: In the year renzi he entered service in Kublai's princely domain.
translations.idiomatic: In renzi (1252) he entered service in Kublai's princely household.

sentences.zh: 王鶚嘗言詩，因問文忠能之乎，文忠曰：「吾少讀書，惟知入則孝於親，出則忠於君而已。

translations.literal: Wang E once spoke on poetry and asked whether Wenzhong could do it; Wenzhong said: "In my youth I read books and knew only that entering one should be filial to parents and going out loyal to the ruler—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E once spoke on poetry and asked whether Wenzhong could compose. Wenzhong said, "In youth I read books and knew only this: at home be filial to one's parents, abroad be loyal to one's lord.

sentences.zh: 詩非所學也。」

translations.literal: Poetry is not what I studied."
translations.idiomatic: Poetry is not what I studied."

sentences.zh: 癸丑，從征南詔。

translations.literal: In guichou he followed the southern-campaign edict.
translations.idiomatic: In guichou (1253) he followed the edict for the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 己未，伐宋，與兄文炳、文用敗宋兵於陽羅堡，得蒙衝百艘，進圍鄂。

translations.literal: In jiwei, attacking Song, together with his elder brothers Wenbing and Wenyong he defeated Song troops at Yangluo Fort, seized a hundred warships, and advanced to besiege E.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei (1259), on the Song campaign, he and his brothers Wenbing and Wenyong routed Song forces at Yangluo Fort, captured a hundred warships, and advanced to besiege Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，侍講學士徒單公履欲奏行貢舉，知帝於釋氏重教而輕禪，乃言儒亦有之，科舉類教，道學類禪。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Lecturing Academician Tuan Gonglu wished to memorialize implementing the civil examinations; knowing the emperor in Buddhism valued teaching and slighted Chan, he said Confucianism had the same—the examinations resemble teaching, Neo-Confucian philosophy resembles Chan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1271) Lecturing Academician Tuan Gonglu wished to memorialize for civil examinations. Knowing Kublai in Buddhism valued teaching over Chan meditation, he argued that Confucianism had the same split: civil examinations were like teaching, Neo-Confucian philosophy like Chan.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，召姚樞、許衡與宰臣廷辨。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and summoned Yao Shu, Xu Heng, and the chief ministers for court debate.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai grew angry and summoned Yao Shu, Xu Heng, and the chief ministers for a court debate.

sentences.zh: 文忠自外入，帝曰：「汝日誦四書，亦道學者。」

translations.literal: Wenzhong entered from outside; the emperor said: "You daily recite the Four Books—you too are a Neo-Confucian."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong came in from outside. Kublai said, "You recite the Four Books every day—you too are a Neo-Confucian."

sentences.zh: 文忠對曰：「陛下每言：士不治經講孔孟之道而為詩賦，何關修身，何益治國！

translations.literal: Wenzhong replied: "Your Majesty has often said: scholars who do not govern the classics and expound the way of Confucius and Mencius but compose poetry and rhapsodies—what has that to do with cultivating the person, what benefit for governing the state!
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong replied, "Your Majesty has often said that scholars who neglect the classics and the way of Confucius and Mencius to write poetry and rhapsodies neither cultivate the person nor help govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 由是海內之士，稍知從事實學。

translations.literal: From this scholars throughout the realm gradually knew to pursue practical learning.
translations.idiomatic: From that the scholars of the realm gradually turned to practical learning.

sentences.zh: 臣今所誦，皆孔孟之言，焉知所謂道學！

translations.literal: What your subject now recites is all the words of Confucius and Mencius—how would I know what is called Neo-Confucianism!
translations.idiomatic: What I recite now is the word of Confucius and Mencius—how should I know anything of Neo-Confucianism!

sentences.zh: 而俗儒守亡國餘習，欲行其說，故以是上惑聖聽，恐非陛下教人修身治國之意也。」

translations.literal: Yet vulgar Confucians cling to the surviving habits of a fallen state, wishing to impose their doctrines—therefore they thus delude the sacred hearing above; I fear this is not Your Majesty's intent in teaching people to cultivate the person and govern the state."
translations.idiomatic: Yet shallow scholars cling to the bad habits of a fallen dynasty and wish to impose their doctrine, thereby misleading Your Majesty. I fear that is not your intent in teaching self-cultivation and good government."

sentences.zh: 事遂止。

translations.literal: The matter then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十一年，伐宋，民困供饋，文忠奏免常歲橫征，從之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, attacking Song, the people were distressed by provisioning; Wenzhong memorialized exemption from the annual irregular levies; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1274), as the Song campaign strained the people's provisioning, Wenzhong memorialized to abolish the annual irregular levies, and Kublai agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗見宋降將，從容問宋所以亡者，皆曰：「賈似道當國，薄武人而重文儒，將士怨之，莫有鬪志。

translations.literal: The emperor once received Song surrendering generals and, at ease, asked why Song had perished; all said: "When Jia Sidao held the state he slighted fighting men and favored literati; officers and soldiers resented it and none had fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai once received surrendered Song generals and asked casually why Song had fallen. They all said, "Jia Sidao held power, slighted military men, and favored literati. Officers and soldiers resented him and had no will to fight.

sentences.zh: 故大軍既至，爭解甲歸命也。」

translations.literal: Therefore when the great army arrived they vied to doff armor and submit."
translations.idiomatic: So when the Great Army arrived they were eager to lay down arms and submit."

sentences.zh: 帝問文忠：「此言何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Wenzhong: "What of this speech?"
translations.idiomatic: Kublai asked Wenzhong, "What do you make of this?"

sentences.zh: 文忠因詰之曰：「似道薄汝矣，而君則貴汝以官，富汝以祿，未嘗薄汝也。

translations.literal: Wenzhong thereupon pressed them: "Sidao slighted you—but your lord honored you with office and enriched you with stipend; he never slighted you.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong pressed them: "Sidao slighted you—but your emperor ennobled you with office and enriched you with stipend. He did not slight you.

sentences.zh: 今有怨於相，而移於君，不肯一戰，坐視國亡，如臣節何！

translations.literal: Now you harbor resentment against the chancellor yet shift it to your lord, refuse to fight once, and sit watching the state perish—what of the integrity of a subject!
translations.idiomatic: You resent the chancellor yet turn on your emperor, refuse to fight, and sit idle while the realm falls—what kind of loyalty is that!

sentences.zh: 然則似道薄汝者，豈非預知汝曹不足恃乎！」

translations.literal: Then was not Sidao's slighting of you precisely because he foreknew you lot could not be relied upon!"
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps Sidao slighted you because he already knew you could not be relied upon!"

sentences.zh: 帝深善之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai greatly approved.

sentences.zh: 有旨徙大都獵戶於郢中，文忠奏止之。

translations.literal: There was an order to relocate the Dadu hunting households to Ying; Wenzhong memorialized to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the relocation of Dadu hunting households to Ying. Wenzhong memorialized against it.

sentences.zh: 又請罷官鬻田器之稅，聽民自為。

translations.literal: He also requested abolishing the official tax on selling farming tools, allowing the people to make their own.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to abolish the tax on farm implements sold by officials and let the people make their own.

sentences.zh: 時多盜，詔犯者皆殺無赦。

translations.literal: At the time there were many thieves; an edict ordered that offenders all be killed without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Theft was rampant, and an edict ordered that all offenders be executed without mercy.

sentences.zh: 在處繫囚滿獄。

translations.literal: Everywhere the imprisoned filled the jails.
translations.idiomatic: Jails everywhere were overflowing.

sentences.zh: 文忠言：「殺人取貨，與竊一錢者均死，慘黷莫甚，恐乖陛下好生之德。」

translations.literal: Wenzhong said: "Killing for goods and stealing a single cash coin receive the same death—nothing could be more cruel and profane; I fear this goes against Your Majesty's virtue of cherishing life."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong said, "To punish murder for plunder and theft of a single cash alike with death is cruel beyond measure. I fear this violates Your Majesty's virtue of cherishing life."

sentences.zh: 敕革之。

translations.literal: An edict reformed it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict revised the policy.

sentences.zh: 或告漢人毆傷國人，及太府監屬盧甲盜剪官布。

translations.literal: Someone reported that a Han man had beaten and injured a subject of the realm, and that Lu Jia, an officer of the Grand Provisioner's Office, had stolen and cut official cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that a Han man had beaten a Mongol subject, and that Lu Jia, an officer of the Grand Provisioner's Office, had stolen and cut official cloth.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命殺以懲衆。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered them killed to warn the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai was enraged and ordered them executed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 文忠言：「今刑曹於囚罪當死者，已有服辭，猶必詳讞，是豈可因人一言，遽加之重典！

translations.literal: Wenzhong said: "Now the penal offices, even for prisoners whose crime warrants death and who have confessed, still must fully try the case—is it permissible on one person's word suddenly to impose the heavy penalty!
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong said, "Even when a condemned prisoner has confessed, the penal offices must still examine the case carefully. How can we impose capital punishment on a single informer's word!

sentences.zh: 宜付有司閱實，以俟後命。」

translations.literal: They should be handed to the proper offices to verify, awaiting further command."
translations.idiomatic: The matter should go to the proper offices for verification, pending Your Majesty's further order."

sentences.zh: 乃遣文忠及近臣突滿分覈之，皆得其誣狀，遂詔原之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wenzhong and the close attendant Tuman were sent to investigate separately; both cases proved false accusation, and an edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai sent Wenzhong and the close attendant Tuman to investigate separately. Both cases proved to be false accusations, and an edict pardoned the accused.

sentences.zh: 帝因責侍臣曰：「方朕怒時，卿曹皆不敢言。

translations.literal: The emperor then rebuked his attendants: "When I was angry you all dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai then rebuked his attendants: "When I was angry, none of you dared speak.

sentences.zh: 非董文忠開悟朕心，則殺二無辜之人，必取議中外矣。」

translations.literal: Had not Dong Wenzhong opened my mind, two innocent men would have been killed and criticism would surely have been taken from within and without the court."
translations.idiomatic: Had not Dong Wenzhong opened my mind, two innocent men would have died and the court would have faced reproach at home and abroad."

sentences.zh: 因賜文忠金尊，曰：「用旌卿直。」

translations.literal: He therefore granted Wenzhong a gold goblet, saying: "To honor your integrity."
translations.idiomatic: He granted Wenzhong a gold goblet, saying, "To honor your integrity."

sentences.zh: 裕宗亦語宮臣曰：「方天威之震，董文忠從容諫正，實人臣難能者。」

translations.literal: Prince Yu also told palace officials: "When imperial majesty flared, Dong Wenzhong calmly admonished and corrected—truly what is difficult for a subject."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu told palace officials, "When imperial wrath flared, Dong Wenzhong calmly corrected him—a feat few subjects could manage."

sentences.zh: 太府監屬奉物詣文忠泣謝曰：「鄙人賴公復生。」

translations.literal: The Grand Provisioner's officer brought gifts to Wenzhong, weeping thanks: "This humble man owes his renewed life to you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Provisioner's officer brought gifts to Wenzhong and wept his thanks: "I owe my life to you, sir."

sentences.zh: 文忠曰：「吾素非知子，所以相救於危急者，蓋為國平刑，豈望子見報哉！」

translations.literal: Wenzhong said: "I have not known you before; the reason I rescued you in crisis was simply to level punishments for the state—how could I expect repayment from you!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong said, "I did not know you before. I acted because the state must see justice done—not because I expected anything from you!"

sentences.zh: 却其物不受。

translations.literal: He refused the gifts and would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the gifts.

sentences.zh: 自安童北伐，阿合馬獨當國柄，大立親黨，懼廉希憲復入為相，害其私計，奏希憲以右丞行省江陵。

translations.literal: Since Antong's northern campaign Ahmad alone held the reins of state, greatly establishing his own faction; fearing Lian Xixian would return as chancellor and harm his private designs, he memorialized that Xixian go as Right Vice Chancellor to administer Jiangling province.
translations.idiomatic: After Antong marched north, Ahmad alone held power and built a private faction. Fearing Lian Xixian might return as chancellor and thwart his schemes, he memorialized to send Xixian to Jiangling as Right Vice Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 文忠言：「希憲，國家名臣。

translations.literal: Wenzhong said: "Xixian is a famed minister of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong said, "Xixian is one of the state's foremost ministers.

sentences.zh: 今宰相虛位，不可使久居外，以孤人望，宜早召還。」

translations.literal: Now the chancellorship sits vacant; he cannot be kept long abroad, isolating people's hopes—he should be summoned back soon."
translations.idiomatic: The chancellorship is vacant; he should not be kept abroad and cut off from public expectation. Summon him back soon."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai agreed.

sentences.zh: 十六年十月，奏曰：「陛下始以燕王為中書令、樞密使，纔一至中書。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixteenth year he memorialized: "Your Majesty first made the Prince of Yan chancellor of the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs; he has come to the Secretariat only once.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the sixteenth year (1279) he memorialized: "Your Majesty first made the Prince of Yan chancellor of the Secretariat and military commissioner, but he has attended the Secretariat only once.

sentences.zh: 自冊為太子，累使明習軍國之事，然十有餘年，終守謙退，不肯視事者，非不奉明詔也，蓋朝廷處之未盡其道爾。

translations.literal: Since investiture as heir apparent repeated orders have made him clearly study military and state affairs, yet for more than ten years he has always kept humility and retreat, refusing to handle affairs—not because he does not obey bright edicts, but because the court has not fully applied the proper way.
translations.idiomatic: Since his investiture as heir you have repeatedly ordered him to learn state and military affairs. Yet for more than ten years he has remained modest and declined to take charge—not from disobedience, but because the court has not handled the matter properly.

sentences.zh: 夫事已奏決，而始啟太子，是使臣子而可否君父之命，故惟有唯默避遜而已。

translations.literal: When matters have already been memorialized and decided and only then opened to the heir apparent, this makes a subject approve or reject the lord-father's command—thus he can only keep silence and yield.
translations.idiomatic: When matters are decided before they reach the heir, a subject would be judging his father's commands. No wonder he can only keep silent and hold back.

sentences.zh: 以臣所知，不若令有司先啟而後聞，其有未安者，則以詔敕斷之，庶幾理順而分不踰，太子必不敢辭其責矣。」

translations.literal: In your subject's understanding, it would be better to have the offices first report and only afterward inform him; if anything is unsettled, let edict decide—then principle will be ordered and roles not exceeded, and the heir will not dare shirk responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: In my view, let the offices report to him first and then inform Your Majesty. What remains unsettled let edict decide. Then roles will be clear and the heir will not dare shirk his duty."

sentences.zh: 帝即日召大臣，面諭其意，使行之。

translations.literal: That day the emperor summoned the chief ministers, face to face expounding his intent, and had it put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Kublai summoned the chief ministers, explained his intent, and put the plan into practice.

sentences.zh: 復語太子曰：「董八，崇立國本者，其勿忘之。」

translations.literal: He further told the heir: "Dong Ba—who upheld the foundation of the state—do not forget him."
translations.idiomatic: He told the heir, "Dong Ba upheld the foundation of the realm—do not forget him."

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書謝昌元請立門下省，封駁制敕，以絕中書風曉近習奏請之弊。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Xie Changyuan requested establishing a Gate Department to seal and reject edicts, to cut off the Secretariat's evil of favored intimates submitting petitions at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Xie Changyuan proposed a Gate Department with power to seal and reject edicts, to end the habit of the Secretariat's favored intimates submitting petitions at dawn.

sentences.zh: 帝銳意欲行之，詔廷臣雜議；

translations.literal: The emperor keenly wished to implement it and ordered court ministers to debate jointly;
translations.idiomatic: Kublai was eager to put it into effect and ordered the court to debate the proposal;

sentences.zh: 且怒翰林學士承旨王磐曰：「如是有益之事，汝不入告，而使南方後至之臣言之，汝用學問何為！

translations.literal: and angrily said to Hanlin Academician Chancellor Wang Pan: "On so beneficial a matter you did not first inform me, yet let a southern minister who arrived later speak of it—what use do you make of your learning!
translations.idiomatic: and angrily told Hanlin Academician Chancellor Wang Pan, "On so useful a matter you did not tell me first, but let a southern newcomer speak of it—what do you use your learning for!

sentences.zh: 必今日開是省。」

translations.literal: This department must be opened today."
translations.idiomatic: This department must be opened today."

sentences.zh: 三日，廷臣奏以文忠為侍中，及其屬數十人。

translations.literal: Three days later court ministers memorialized appointing Wenzhong as Attendant-in-Ordinary, and several tens of his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later the court memorialized Wenzhong as Attendant-in-Ordinary, with several dozen subordinates.

sentences.zh: 近臣乘便言曰：「陛下將別置省，此實其時。

translations.literal: A close attendant seized the opportunity and said: "Your Majesty is about to establish a separate department—this is truly the moment.
translations.idiomatic: A close attendant seized the moment: "Your Majesty is about to set up a separate department—now is the time.

sentences.zh: 然得人則可以寬聖心，新民聽；

translations.literal: Yet if the right men are obtained the sacred mind can be eased and the people's hearing refreshed;
translations.idiomatic: But with the right men the emperor's mind can be eased and the people's trust won;

sentences.zh: 今聞盜詐之臣與居其間，不可。」

translations.literal: now I hear that thieving and deceitful subjects would sit among them—it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: yet I hear that thieving, deceitful men would sit among them—that will not do."

sentences.zh: 其言多指文忠。

translations.literal: His words largely pointed at Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His words were largely aimed at Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 文忠忿辨曰：「上每稱臣不盜不詐，今汝顧臣而言，意實在臣。

translations.literal: Wenzhong indignantly rebutted: "Your Majesty often calls me neither thieving nor deceitful—now you look at me as you speak; your intent is truly fixed on me.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong angrily rebutted, "Your Majesty has often said I am neither thief nor fraud—yet you look at me as you speak. Your meaning is plain.

sentences.zh: 其顯言臣盜詐何事！」

translations.literal: If you openly say I thieve and deceive, what is the matter!"
translations.idiomatic: Name plainly what I have stolen or defrauded!"

sentences.zh: 帝令言者出，文忠猶訴不止，且攻其害國之姦。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the speaker out; Wenzhong still appealed without stopping, also attacking his state-harming treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai had the accuser dismissed, but Wenzhong kept protesting and exposed the man's treachery against the state.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕自知之，彼不言汝也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I know it myself—he did not mean you."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "I know the truth—he did not mean you."

sentences.zh: 其人忌文忠，欲中害之，然以文忠清慎無過，乃奉鈔萬緡為壽，求交驩，文忠却之。

translations.literal: That man hated Wenzhong and wished to harm him through entrapment; yet because Wenzhong was pure and careful without fault, he presented ten thousand strings' worth of notes as a birthday gift, seeking reconciliation; Wenzhong refused.
translations.idiomatic: The man hated Wenzhong and sought to ruin him, but finding Wenzhong clean and beyond reproach, sent ten thousand strings of notes as a birthday gift seeking reconciliation. Wenzhong refused.

sentences.zh: 文炳為中書左丞卒，太傅伯顏乃表文忠可相，帝使繼其官，文忠辭曰：「臣兄有平定南方之勞，可居是位。

translations.literal: Wenbing died while Left Vice Chancellor of the Secretariat; Grand Preceptor Bayan then memorialized that Wenzhong could serve as chancellor; the emperor had him succeed to the office; Wenzhong declined: "Your subject's elder brother had the merit of pacifying the south and could hold that post.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenbing died as Left Vice Chancellor, Grand Preceptor Bayan recommended Wenzhong for chancellor. Kublai ordered him to succeed, but Wenzhong declined: "My brother earned the southern pacification. He deserved that rank.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗給事居中，所宣何力，敢冒居重職乎！」

translations.literal: Your subject once served at court center on errands—what force did he exert? How dare he presumptuously occupy a weighty post!"
translations.idiomatic: I merely served at court on errands—what merit had I? How dare I take so weighty a post!"

sentences.zh: 十八年，陞典瑞局為監、郎為卿，仍以文忠為之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Bureau of Imperial Insignia was raised from bureau to directorate, and clerks to directors; Wenzhong still held the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1281) the Bureau of Imperial Insignia was raised to a directorate and its clerks to directors; Wenzhong retained the post.

sentences.zh: 授正議大夫，俄授資德大夫、僉書樞密院事，卿如故。

translations.literal: He was granted Regular Grand Master; soon granted Grand Master for Splendid Virtue and Concurrent Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, director as before.
translations.idiomatic: He received the rank of Regular Grand Master and soon Grand Master for Splendid Virtue with concurrent appointment as secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, retaining the directorship.

sentences.zh: 車駕行幸，詔文忠毋扈從，留居大都，凡宮苑、城門、直舍、徼道、環衛、營屯、禁兵、太府、少府、軍器、尚乘諸監，皆領焉。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage traveled on tour, an edict ordered Wenzhong not to escort but to remain in Dadu; all palace parks, city gates, straight lodgings, patrol paths, encircling guard, garrison camps, forbidden troops, Grand Provisioner, Minor Provisioner, Armory, and Imperial Stud directorates—he oversaw them all.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled, an edict left Wenzhong in Dadu rather than on escort duty. He oversaw palace grounds, gates, lodgings, patrol routes, guard posts, garrisons, forbidden troops, and the directorates of provision, arms, and the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 兵馬司舊隸中書，併付文忠。

translations.literal: The Horse and Chariot Office had formerly been subordinate to the Secretariat; it too was handed over to Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Horse and Chariot Office, formerly under the Secretariat, was also placed under Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 時權臣累請奪還中書，不報。

translations.literal: At the time the powerful minister repeatedly requested to seize back the Secretariat; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful minister at court repeatedly petitioned to restore control of the Secretariat to him, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 是冬十月二十有五日，雞鳴，將入朝，忽病仆，帝遣中使持藥投救不及，遂卒，甚悼惜之，賻錢數十萬。

translations.literal: That winter, on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month, at cockcrow, as he was about to enter court he suddenly fell ill and collapsed; the emperor sent palace emissaries bearing medicine but could not save him in time; he died. The emperor deeply mourned and regretted it and granted funeral money in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month, at cockcrow, as he was about to attend court he suddenly collapsed. The emperor sent palace physicians with medicine, but they could not reach him in time. He died. The emperor mourned him deeply and granted several hundred thousand in funeral funds.

sentences.zh: 後制贈光祿大夫、司徒，封壽國公，諡忠貞。

translations.literal: Later by edict he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Virtue and Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Duke of Shou State, posthumous name Loyal and Upright.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict posthumously granted him Grand Master of Splendid Virtue and Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed him as Duke of Shou State, and gave him the posthumous name Loyal and Upright.

sentences.zh: 嚴實子忠濟 忠嗣

translations.literal: Yan Shi—sons: Zhongji, Zhongsi
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi—his sons Zhongji and Zhongsi

sentences.zh: 嚴實字武叔，泰安長清人。

translations.literal: Yan Shi, courtesy name Wushu, was a native of Changqing in Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi, whose courtesy name was Wushu, came from Changqing in Tai'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 略知書，志氣豪放，不治生產，喜交結施與，落魄里社間。

translations.literal: He had some knowledge of books; his spirit was bold and free. He did not manage production but loved making connections and giving generously, living in shabby freedom among the village community.
translations.idiomatic: He had some learning and a bold, open temperament. He neglected his estate but loved making friends and giving freely, living in rough, unbuttoned fashion among the villages.

sentences.zh: 屢以事繫獄，俠少輩為出死力，乃得脫去。

translations.literal: Repeatedly imprisoned on various charges, young swashbucklers exerted their utmost strength on his behalf, and only then could he escape.
translations.idiomatic: He was jailed again and again on various charges, and only when young men of the sword rallied to him with their lives could he break free.

sentences.zh: 癸酉秋，太祖率兵自紫荊口入，分略山東、河北、河東而歸。

translations.literal: In the autumn of guiyou, Taizu led troops in through Zijing Pass, divided forces to overrun Shandong, Hebei, and Hedong, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of guiyou (1213), Taizu led his army in through Zijing Pass, sent columns to overrun Shandong, Hebei, and Hedong, and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 金東平行臺調民為兵，以實為衆所服，命為百戶。

translations.literal: The Jin Eastern Pacification Circuit mobilized the people as soldiers; since Shi was admired by the masses, he was appointed a centurion commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Eastern Pacification Circuit conscripted the people for war. Shi was admired by the crowd and was made a centurion commander.

sentences.zh: 甲戌春，泰安張汝楫據靈巖，遣別將攻長清，實破走之。

translations.literal: In the spring of jiaxu, Zhang Ruji of Tai'an held Lingyan and sent a subordinate general to attack Changqing; Shi defeated and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of jiaxu (1214), Zhang Ruji of Tai'an held Lingyan and sent a deputy to attack Changqing; Shi routed him and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 以功授長清尉。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed warden of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was appointed warden of Changqing.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，權長清令。

translations.literal: In wuyin, acting magistrate of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: In wuyin (1218) he served as acting magistrate of Changqing.

sentences.zh: 宋取益都，乘勝而西，行臺檄實備芻糧為守禦計。

translations.literal: Song took Yidu and, riding their victory, marched west; the circuit administration ordered Shi to gather fodder and grain for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Song seized Yidu and pressed west on the momentum of victory. The circuit administration ordered Shi to gather fodder and grain for the defense.

sentences.zh: 實出督租，比還，而長清破，俄以兵復之。

translations.literal: Shi went out to supervise tax collection; when he returned, Changqing had fallen, but soon he recovered it by force.
translations.idiomatic: Shi went out to oversee tax collection. By the time he returned, Changqing had fallen, but he soon retook it by force.

sentences.zh: 有譖于行臺者，謂實與宋有謀，行臺以兵圍之，實挈家避青崖。

translations.literal: Someone slandered him to the circuit administration, saying Shi was plotting with Song; the circuit sent troops to surround him; Shi took his family and fled to Qingya.
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered him to the circuit, claiming Shi was plotting with Song. The circuit sent troops to surround him, and Shi fled with his family to Qingya.

sentences.zh: 宋因以實為濟南治中，分兵四出，所至無不下，於是太行之東，皆受實節制。

translations.literal: Song thereupon appointed Shi Adjunct Administrator of Jinan, dispatched troops in four directions—wherever they went nothing failed to fall—thereupon east of the Taihang all submitted to Shi's command.
translations.idiomatic: Song then made Shi Adjunct Administrator of Jinan and sent troops in four directions; wherever they went, cities fell. Thereafter everything east of the Taihang range came under Shi's command.

sentences.zh: 庚辰三月，金河南軍攻彰德，守將單仲力不支，數求救。

translations.literal: In the third month of gengchen, Jin's Henan army attacked Zhangde; the defending general Shan Zhong could not hold and repeatedly begged for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of gengchen (1220), the Jin Henan army attacked Zhangde. The defender Shan Zhong could not hold out and sent repeated pleas for help.

sentences.zh: 實請於主將張林，林逗遛不行，實獨以兵赴之，比至，而仲被擒。

translations.literal: Shi requested permission from the commander in chief Zhang Lin; Lin dallied and would not march; Shi alone led troops to the rescue; by the time he arrived, Zhong had already been captured.
translations.idiomatic: Shi asked the commander in chief Zhang Lin for leave to go, but Lin procrastinated and would not move. Shi marched alone with his troops, and by the time he arrived, Zhong had already been taken.

sentences.zh: 實知宋不足恃。

translations.literal: Shi knew Song was not worth relying on.
translations.idiomatic: Shi knew the Song could not be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 七月，謁太師木華黎於軍門，挈所部彰德、大名、磁、洺、恩、博、滑、濬等州戶三十萬來歸，木華黎承制拜實金紫光祿大夫、行尚書省事。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he paid respects to Grand Preceptor Muqali at the army gate, bringing with him the households of his command from the prefectures Zhangde, Daming, Ci, Ming, En, Bo, Hua, and Jun—three hundred thousand in all—to submit; Muqali, acting by imperial commission, appointed Shi Grand Master of the Gold-and-Purple Light and Acting Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he called on Grand Preceptor Muqali at headquarters and brought the three hundred thousand households under his command from Zhangde, Daming, Ci, Ming, En, Bo, Hua, Jun, and neighboring prefectures to submit. Muqali, acting by imperial commission, made Shi Grand Master of the Gold-and-Purple Light and Acting Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 進攻曹、濮、單三州，皆下之。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack the three prefectures of Cao, Pu, and Shan, he took them all.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against the three prefectures of Cao, Pu, and Shan and took them all.

sentences.zh: 偏將李信，留鎮青崖，嘗有罪，懼誅，乘實之出，殺其家屬，降于宋。

translations.literal: The deputy general Li Xin was left to garrison Qingya. He had once committed a crime and feared execution; taking advantage of Shi's absence, he killed Shi's family members and surrendered to Song.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy general Li Xin was left to garrison Qingya. He had once offended and feared punishment; while Shi was away he killed Shi's family and surrendered to Song.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，實以兵復青崖，擒信誅之。

translations.literal: In xinsi, Shi recovered Qingya by force, captured Xin, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: In xinsi (1221) Shi retook Qingya by force, captured Li Xin, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 進攻東平，金守將和立剛棄城遁，實入居之。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Dongping, the Jin defender Heli Gang abandoned the city and fled; Shi entered and took up residence there.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Dongping. The Jin defender Heli Gang abandoned the city and fled, and Shi entered and made it his seat.

sentences.zh: 壬午，宋將彭義斌率師取京東州縣，實將晁海以青崖降，盡掠實家，義斌軍西下，郡縣多歸之。

translations.literal: In renwu, the Song general Peng Yibin led an army to seize the prefectures and counties of eastern Jingdong. Shi's officer Chao Hai surrendered Qingya; they plundered Shi's household entirely. Yibin's army marched west, and many commanderies and counties submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: In renwu (1222), the Song general Peng Yibin led troops to seize the prefectures and counties of eastern Jingdong. Shi's officer Chao Hai surrendered Qingya and plundered Shi's household clean. As Yibin's army marched west, many commanderies and counties went over to him.

sentences.zh: 乙酉四月，遂圍東平。

translations.literal: In yiyou, the fourth month, they accordingly besieged Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of yiyou (1225) they besieged Dongping.

sentences.zh: 實潛約大將孛里海合兵攻之，兵久不至，城中食且盡，乃與義斌連和。

translations.literal: Shi secretly arranged with the great general Boerhai to combine forces and attack them, but the army did not arrive for a long time; food in the city was nearly gone, so he made peace with Yibin.
translations.idiomatic: Shi secretly arranged with the great general Boerhai to join forces and attack, but the relief army was long in coming and food in the city was nearly exhausted, so he made peace with Yibin.

sentences.zh: 義斌亦欲藉實取河朔，而後圖之，請以兄事實。

translations.literal: Yibin also wished to use Shi to take Heshuo and afterward plan against him; he asked to treat Shi as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yibin also meant to use Shi to seize Heshuo and deal with him afterward; he asked to treat Shi as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 時麾下衆尚數千，義斌聽其自領，而青崖所掠者則留不遣。

translations.literal: At the time the troops under Shi's command still numbered several thousand; Yibin allowed him to lead them himself, but those plundered from Qingya he retained and would not return.
translations.idiomatic: Shi still had several thousand men under his command; Yibin let him keep them, but withheld everything that had been plundered from Qingya and would not return it.

sentences.zh: 七月，義斌下真定，道西山，與孛里海等軍相望，分實以帳下兵，陽助而陰伺之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Yibin took Zhending, went by the Western Hills, and his army and Boerhai's faced each other from afar. He detached Shi's personal troops, ostensibly to assist but secretly to watch him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yibin took Zhending and marched by the Western Hills until his army and Boerhai's were within sight of each other. He detached Shi's personal troops, ostensibly to help but in secret to keep watch on him.

sentences.zh: 實知勢迫，急赴孛里海軍與之合，遂與義斌戰，宋兵潰，擒義斌。

translations.literal: Shi knew the pressure was extreme; he hurried to Boerhai's army and joined with it, then fought Yibin. The Song army collapsed; Yibin was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the situation tighten, Shi rushed to Boerhai's army and joined him, then gave battle to Yibin. The Song force collapsed and Yibin was captured.

sentences.zh: 不旬月，京東州縣復為實有。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days, the prefectures and counties of eastern Jingdong were again Shi's.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the prefectures and counties of eastern Jingdong were Shi's again.

sentences.zh: 是冬，木華黎之弟帶孫取彰德；

translations.literal: That winter Muqali's younger brother Taisun took Zhangde;
translations.idiomatic: That winter Muqali's younger brother Taisun took Zhangde;

sentences.zh: 明年，取濮、東平；

translations.literal: The next year he took Pu and Dongping;
translations.idiomatic: The next year he took Pu and Dongping;

sentences.zh: 又明年，木華黎之子孛魯取益都：實皆有功焉。

translations.literal: The year after that Muqali's son Bolu took Yidu: Shi had merit in all these.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that Muqali's son Bolu took Yidu—and Shi had a hand in all of these.

sentences.zh: 庚寅四月，朝太宗于牛心之幄殿，帝賜之坐，宴享終日，賜以虎符。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of gengyin he had audience with Taizong at the canopied hall on Niu Mountain; the emperor granted him a seat, feasted him for the whole day, and bestowed a tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of gengyin (1230) he had audience with Ögedei Khan at the canopied hall on Niu Mountain. The emperor gave him a seat, feasted him all day, and bestowed a tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 數顧實謂侍臣曰：「嚴實，真福人也。」

translations.literal: Repeatedly turning to Shi he told the attending ministers: "Yan Shi is truly a man of fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Shi again and again, he told the attending ministers, "Yan Shi is truly a fortunate man."

sentences.zh: 甲午，朝于和林，授東平路行軍萬戶，偏裨賜金符者八人。

translations.literal: In jiawu he had audience at Karakorum; he was appointed mobile corps commander of the Dongping Circuit, and eight subordinate officers were granted gold tallies.
translations.idiomatic: In jiawu (1234) he had audience at Karakorum and was appointed mobile corps commander of the Dongping Circuit; eight of his subordinate officers received gold tallies.

sentences.zh: 先是，實之所統，凡五十餘城，至是，惟德、兗、濟、單隸東平。

translations.literal: Previously what Shi had commanded comprised more than fifty cities; now only De, Yan, Ji, and Shan were subordinated to Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Shi had governed more than fifty cities; now only De, Yan, Ji, and Shan were placed under Dongping.

sentences.zh: 丁酉九月，詔實毋事征伐。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of dingyou an edict ordered that Shi need not engage in campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of dingyou (1237) an edict relieved Shi of further campaigning.

sentences.zh: 初，彰德既下，又破水柵，帶孫怒其反覆，驅老幼數萬欲屠之。

translations.literal: At first, after Zhangde had fallen they also broke the water palisade; Taisun, angry at their back-and-forth, drove tens of thousands of old and young intending to slaughter them.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhangde fell they also broke the water palisade. Taisun, furious at the people's shifting loyalties, drove tens of thousands of old and young together intending to slaughter them.

sentences.zh: 實曰：「此國家舊民，吾兵力不能及，為所脅從，果何罪耶！」

translations.literal: Shi said: "These are old subjects of the state. My military strength could not reach them; they were coerced into following—what crime is that!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "These are long-standing subjects of the realm. My troops could not reach them in time; they were forced to follow—what crime is that!"

sentences.zh: 帶孫從之。

translations.literal: Taisun followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Taisun accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 繼破濮州，復欲屠之。

translations.literal: Afterward they took Pu Prefecture and again wished to slaughter the people.
translations.idiomatic: After Pu Prefecture was taken they again meant to slaughter the population.

sentences.zh: 實言：「百姓未嘗敵我，豈可與執兵刃者同戮，不若留之，以供芻秣。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "The common people never opposed us—how can they be slaughtered like those who bore arms? It is better to keep them to supply fodder."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "The common people never fought us—how can they be killed like armed soldiers? Better to keep them to supply fodder."

sentences.zh: 濮人免者又數萬。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of people of Pu were spared again.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of people in Pu were spared.

sentences.zh: 其後於曹、楚丘、定陶、上黨皆然。

translations.literal: Thereafter at Cao, Chuqiu, Dingtao, and Shangdang it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he did the same at Cao, Chuqiu, Dingtao, and Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 時兵由武關出襄、鄧，實在徐、邳間，以為河南破，屠戮必多，乃載金繒往贖之，且約束諸將，毋敢妄有殺掠。

translations.literal: At that time the army went out through Wuguan toward Xiang and Deng; Shi was between Xu and Pi and thought that when Henan fell slaughter would be heavy. He loaded gold and silks to ransom people and also restrained the generals, forbidding reckless killing and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the army marched out through Wuguan toward Xiang and Deng. Shi was between Xu and Pi and foresaw that when Henan fell the slaughter would be great. He sent gold and silks to ransom captives and ordered the generals not to kill or plunder at will.

sentences.zh: 靈壁一縣，當誅者五萬人，實悉救之。

translations.literal: In Lingbi county alone, fifty thousand were slated for execution; Shi saved them all.
translations.idiomatic: In Lingbi county alone, fifty thousand were marked for execution; Shi saved them all.

sentences.zh: 會大饑，民北徙者多餓死。

translations.literal: There came a great famine; many people fleeing north starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: A great famine followed, and many people fleeing north starved to death.

sentences.zh: 又法，藏匿逃者，保社皆坐。

translations.literal: There was also a law that hiding fugitives made the mutual-responsibility groups liable.
translations.idiomatic: The law also held mutual-responsibility groups liable for hiding fugitives.

sentences.zh: 逃亡無所託，殭尸蔽野，實命作糜粥，盛置道傍，全活者衆。

translations.literal: With nowhere to take refuge, corpses littered the wilds; Shi ordered gruel made and set out in abundance by the roadside; many were preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: With nowhere to flee, corpses covered the fields. Shi ordered gruel prepared and set out in heaps by the roadsides, and many lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 實部曲有逃歸益都者數十人，益都破，皆獲之，以為必殺，實置不問。

translations.literal: Several tens of men from Shi's retinue who had fled back to Yidu were captured when Yidu fell; thinking they would surely be killed, Shi set the matter aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen men from Shi's retinue who had fled to Yidu were captured when Yidu fell. Everyone expected them to be executed, but Shi let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 王義深者，義斌之別將，聞義斌敗，將奔河南，實族屬在東平者，皆為所害。

translations.literal: Wang Yishen had been a subordinate general of Yibin; hearing of Yibin's defeat he was about to flee to Henan. Shi's clansmen at Dongping were all harmed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yishen, a subordinate general of Peng Yibin, heard of Yibin's defeat and was about to flee to Henan. He had harmed all of Shi's kin who were at Dongping.

sentences.zh: 河南破，實獲義深妻子，厚周卹之，送還鄉里，終不以舊怨為嫌。

translations.literal: When Henan fell Shi captured Yishen's wife and children, treated them generously with support, and sent them back to their home district—never holding old grudges against them.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan fell Shi captured Yishen's wife and children, treated them generously, and sent them home—never letting old enmity stand in the way.

sentences.zh: 其寬厚長者類若此。

translations.literal: His generous and elder-like conduct was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His generous, elder-like conduct was of this kind throughout.

sentences.zh: 庚子卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: In gengzi he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in gengzi (1240), aged fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 遠近悲悼，野哭巷祭，旬月不已。

translations.literal: Near and far mourned him; wild weeping and alley sacrifices continued for a full month without cease.
translations.idiomatic: People near and far mourned him; weeping in the fields and offerings in the lanes went on for a month without end.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，追封實為魯國公，諡武惠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong, Shi was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lu State with posthumous name Martial and Gracious.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong (1261) Shi was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lu with the posthumous name Martial and Gracious.

sentences.zh: 子忠貞，金紫光祿大夫；

translations.literal: His son Zhongzhen, Grand Master of the Gold-and-Purple Light;
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongzhen, Grand Master of the Gold-and-Purple Light;

sentences.zh: 忠濟，忠嗣，忠範，忠傑，忠裕，忠祐。

translations.literal: Zhongji, Zhongsi, Zhongfan, Zhongjie, Zhongyu, Zhongyou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji, Zhongsi, Zhongfan, Zhongjie, Zhongyu, and Zhongyou.

sentences.zh: 忠濟，一名忠翰，字紫芝，實之第二子也。

translations.literal: Zhongji, also named Zhonghan, courtesy name Zizhi, was Shi's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji, also called Zhonghan and courtesy name Zizhi, was Shi's second son.

sentences.zh: 儀觀雄偉，善騎射。

translations.literal: His bearing was imposing and he excelled at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: He had an imposing presence and excelled at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，從其父入見太宗，命佩虎符，襲東平路行軍萬戶、管民長官，開府布政，一法其父。

translations.literal: In xinchou he followed his father to audience with Taizong; he was ordered to wear the tiger tally, succeeding as mobile corps commander of the Dongping Circuit and civilian administrator, opening a headquarters and governing by the same methods as his father.
translations.idiomatic: In xinchou (1241) he followed his father to audience with Ögedei Khan, was ordered to wear the tiger tally, and succeeded as mobile corps commander of the Dongping Circuit and civilian administrator. He opened a headquarters and governed by his father's methods.

sentences.zh: 養老尊賢，治為諸道第一。

translations.literal: Supporting the aged and honoring the worthy, his governance ranked first among all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He supported the aged and honored the worthy, and his governance ranked first among all circuits.

sentences.zh: 領兵略地淮、漢，偏裨部曲，戮力用命。

translations.literal: Leading troops to overrun the Huai and Han regions, his deputies and retainers strove with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Leading troops to overrun the Huai and Han regions, his deputies and retainers fought with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 定宗、憲宗即位之始，皆加褒寵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the accession of Dingzong and Xianzong, honors and favors were heaped upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Güyük and Möngke first took the throne, both heaped honors upon him.

sentences.zh: 忠濟初統千戶十有七，乙卯，朝命括新軍山東，益兵二萬有奇。

translations.literal: At first Zhongji commanded seventeen chilies; in yimao the court ordered a levy of new troops in Shandong, increasing his force by more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhongji commanded seventeen chiliarchies. In yimao (1255) the court ordered a levy of new troops in Shandong, adding more than twenty thousand to his force.

sentences.zh: 忠濟弟忠嗣、忠範為萬戶，以次諸弟暨勳將之子為千戶，城戍宿州、蘄縣，而忠濟皆統之。

translations.literal: Zhongji's younger brothers Zhongsi and Zhongfan became commanders; in succession the other brothers and sons of meritorious generals became chiliarchs. They garrisoned fortresses at Suzhou and Qixian, all under Zhongji's overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji's brothers Zhongsi and Zhongfan became commanders; his other brothers and the sons of meritorious generals became chiliarchs in turn. They garrisoned Suzhou and Qixian, all under Zhongji's overall command.

sentences.zh: 己未，世祖南伐，詔率師由間道會鄂。

translations.literal: In jiwei Kublai marched south against Song; an edict ordered him to lead his army by a hidden route to rendezvous at E.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei (1259) Kublai marched south against Song. An edict ordered Zhongji to lead his army by a hidden route to rendezvous at E.

sentences.zh: 親率勇士，梯衝登城。

translations.literal: He personally led brave warriors, scaling the walls with siege ladders and rams.
translations.idiomatic: He personally led brave men up the walls with scaling ladders and battering rams.

sentences.zh: 師還，忠濟選勇敢二千，別命千戶將之，甲仗精銳，所向無前。

translations.literal: When the army returned Zhongji selected two thousand bold men and separately appointed chiliarchs to lead them; their armor and weapons were fine and sharp, and wherever they went none could stand before them.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned Zhongji picked two thousand bold fighters and appointed chiliarchs to lead them separately. Their arms were fine and sharp, and wherever they went none could stand before them.

sentences.zh: 大臣有言其威權太盛者。

translations.literal: Some ministers said his authority was too great.
translations.idiomatic: Some ministers said his power had grown too great.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，召還京師，命忠範代之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he was recalled to the capital; Zhongfan was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong (1261) he was recalled to the capital and Zhongfan was ordered to replace him.

sentences.zh: 忠濟治東平日，借貸於人，代部民納逋賦，歲久愈多。

translations.literal: While governing Dongping, Zhongji borrowed from others to pay overdue taxes on behalf of the people under his command; over the years the debt grew ever larger.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Dongping, Zhongji borrowed money to pay overdue taxes for the people under his command, and over the years the debt grew ever larger.

sentences.zh: 及謝事，債家執文券來徵。

translations.literal: When he left office, creditors came with written bonds to collect.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office, creditors came with written bonds to collect payment.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，悉命發內藏代償。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he ordered payment in full from the imperial storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he ordered the full amount paid from the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 東平廟學故隘陋，改卜高爽地于城東，教養諸生，後多顯者。

translations.literal: The temple school of Dongping was formerly narrow and shabby; he chose high, open ground east of the city and moved it, nourishing and teaching students—many later became eminent men.
translations.idiomatic: Dongping's temple school had been cramped and shabby. He chose high, open ground east of the city and moved it there, educating students—many later rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 幕僚如宋子貞、劉肅、李昶、徐世隆，俱為名臣。

translations.literal: Staff members such as Song Zizhen, Liu Su, Li Chang, and Xu Shilong all became renowned ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Staff members such as Song Zizhen, Liu Su, Li Chang, and Xu Shilong all became celebrated ministers.

sentences.zh: 至元二十三年，特授資德大夫、中書左丞、行江浙省事，以老辭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Zhiyuan he was specially appointed Grand Master for Supporting Virtue, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Acting Director of Jiang-Zhe Affairs; he declined on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Zhiyuan (1286) he was specially appointed Grand Master for Supporting Virtue, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Acting Director of Jiang-Zhe Affairs, but declined on account of age.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，賜鈔萬五千緡、宅一區，召其子瑜入侍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was granted ten thousand five hundred strings of paper money and one residence; his son Yu was summoned to attend at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (1292) he was granted fifteen thousand strings of paper money and a residence, and his son Yu was summoned to attend at court.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1293) he died.

sentences.zh: 忠濟統理方郡凡十一年，爵人命官，生殺予奪，皆自己出。

translations.literal: Zhongji governed the region for eleven years in all; ennoblements, appointments, life and death, reward and punishment—all issued from his own decision.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji governed the region for eleven years in all. Ennoblements, appointments, and the power of life, death, reward, and punishment all issued from his own hand.

sentences.zh: 及謝去大權，貴而能貧，安于義命，世以是多之。

translations.literal: After surrendering great power he was noble yet could be poor, content with fate's decree; the world therefore praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: After giving up great power he remained noble yet lived in poverty, content with his lot—and the world praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 後諡莊孝。

translations.literal: Later he was given posthumous name Solemn and Filial.
translations.idiomatic: He was later given the posthumous name Solemn and Filial.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣，實之第三子也。

translations.literal: Zhongsi was Shi's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi was Shi's third son.

sentences.zh: 少從張澄、商挺、李楨學，略知經史大義。

translations.literal: In youth he studied with Zhang Cheng, Shang Ting, and Li Zhen and gained some understanding of the broad meaning of the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied with Zhang Cheng, Shang Ting, and Li Zhen and gained some grasp of the broad meaning of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，其兄忠濟授以東平人匠緫管，遙領單州防禦使事。

translations.literal: In xinhai his elder brother Zhongji appointed him overall manager of Dongping's artisan households, remotely overseeing the defense of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In xinhai (1251) his elder brother Zhongji appointed him overall manager of Dongping's artisan households and gave him remote charge of the defense of Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，充東平路管軍萬戶。

translations.literal: In yimao he filled the post of mobile corps commander of Dongping Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In yimao (1255) he became mobile corps commander of the Dongping Circuit.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，從忠濟略地揚州，取邵伯埭，首立戰功。

translations.literal: In dingsi he followed Zhongji to overrun Yangzhou, took Shaobo Dam, and was first to establish merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In dingsi (1257) he followed Zhongji in overrunning Yangzhou, took Shaobo Dam, and was first to distinguish himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 己未南征，從忠濟渡淮，分兵出挂車嶺，與宋兵相拒三晝夜，殺獲甚衆，始達蘄州。

translations.literal: In the southern expedition of jiwei he followed Zhongji across the Huai, divided his force to go out through Guache Ridge, and faced Song troops for three days and nights, killing and capturing a great many before reaching Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern expedition of jiwei (1259) he followed Zhongji across the Huai, sent a detachment out through Guache Ridge, and fought Song troops for three days and nights, killing and capturing many before reaching Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 及渡江抵鄂，分部攻城九十餘日，戰甚力。

translations.literal: After crossing the river and reaching E, he was detached to besiege the city for more than ninety days and fought with great force.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Yangzi and reaching E, he was detached to besiege the city for more than ninety days and fought fiercely.

sentences.zh: 師還，授金虎符。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was granted a gold tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was granted a gold tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，李璮叛，宋兵攻蘄縣，勢張甚，徐州緫管李杲哥降于宋，齊魯山寨為宋兵所據。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong Li Tan rebelled; Song troops attacked Qixian with overwhelming force; Xuzhou commander Liguo surrendered to Song and the mountain strongholds of Qi and Lu were occupied by Song troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhongtong (1262) Li Tan rebelled. Song troops attacked Qixian with great force. Xuzhou commander Liguo surrendered to Song, and the mountain strongholds of Qi and Lu fell to Song troops.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣從大帥按脫救蘄縣，復徐州，執李杲哥殺之。

translations.literal: Zhongsi followed the chief commander Antu to relieve Qixian, recovered Xuzhou, captured Liguo, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi followed the chief commander Antu to relieve Qixian, retook Xuzhou, captured Liguo, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 攻鄒之嶧山、滕之牙山，多所殺獲。

translations.literal: Attacking Yishan in Zou and Yashan in Teng, he killed and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking Yishan in Zou and Yashan in Teng, he killed and captured many.

sentences.zh: 按脫論功以聞，賜銀二百兩、幣五十端。

translations.literal: Antu reported the merits to the court; he was granted two hundred taels of silver and fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Antu reported his merits to the court, and he was granted two hundred taels of silver and fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 四年，朝廷懲青齊之亂，居大藩者，子弟不得親政，於是罷官家居。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the court, punishing the turmoil in Qing and Qi, decreed that those holding great fiefs could not let their sons administer directly; Zhongsi was therefore dismissed and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1263) the court, reacting to the turmoil in Qing and Qi, ruled that holders of great fiefs could not let their sons govern directly. Zhongsi was therefore dismissed and lived at home.

sentences.zh: 至元十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Zhiyuan (1273).
